title: The recorder panel
description: Set up a recording in the New Recording panel, from what to record and where it lands to what each control does and what the panel remembers.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The New Recording panel holds every recording choice in one place: record a display, a window, a camera or the microphone, straight into a project.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording… on the Welcome window"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The macOS permission for what you record, asked for when you press Record."
/>

## Open the panel

Choose **File ▸ New Recording…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>, or click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). You don't need a project open, and the menu item is always available.

There's one panel for the whole app. A recording doesn't belong to a project window, so it carries on if you close one.

While a recording runs, paused included, the same menu item reads **File ▸ Stop Recording** and <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> stops the recording. The Welcome window's button never stops one: during a screen recording you started in the panel it beeps, and during a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording it shows the panel.

33	## Make a recording
34	
35	<Steps>
36	
37	1. Choose what to record in [**Source**](#choose-a-source).
38	
39	2. Choose where it goes in [**Record Into**](#choose-where-it-lands).
40	
41	3. Set any other [controls](#the-controls). Rows that don't apply to your source are greyed out.
42	
43	4. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) that source needs, then counts down from 3.
44	
45	5. Stop when you're done. See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/).
46	
47	</Steps>
48	
49	**Close** closes the panel without recording.
50	
51	A recording is saved as an ordinary movie or audio file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, then imported like any other media, so every edit, effect and export works on it. When you stop, it [lands](/recording/where-it-lands/): it's placed at the playhead of the project you chose, or opens as a new project.
52	
53	## Choose a source
54	
55	**Source** lists one row for each connected display, by name, and then three more.
56	
57	| Row | What it records |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| A display's name | [The whole display](/recording/record-a-display/). |
60	| **Window…** | [One window](/recording/record-a-window/), which you pick with macOS's window picker. |
61	| **Camera** | [A camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/), with no screen. |
62	| **Microphone Only** | [A voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/): the microphone with no picture. |
63	
64	It starts on the display you used last, or the main display if there isn't one. Every display is listed even before Frame Job has the Screen Recording permission, so the panel can open and tell you what's missing.
65	
66	To record a camera as well as the screen, keep a display or **Window…** as the source and tick **Record the camera too**. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).
67	
68	## Choose where it lands
69	
70	**Record Into** lists **New Project** first, then every open project by name. It starts on the project in front, or **New Project** when none is open.
71	
72	The row follows whichever project is in front until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open, and if you close the project it goes back to following the one in front. If you choose **New Project**, it stays there.
73	
74	The list updates every second while the panel is idle. From the moment you press **Record** until the recording has landed it's frozen, so clicking into another project during a recording doesn't change where the recording goes.
75	
76	**Record Into** is never remembered between launches.
77	
78	## The controls
79	
80	These are the panel's rows in order, with what each starts on before you've changed anything.
81	
82	| Control | What it does | Default |
83	| --- | --- | --- |
84	| **Source** | [What to record](#choose-a-source). | The main display |
85	| **Include Frame Job windows** | [Puts Frame Job's own windows](/recording/record-a-display/#include-frame-job-windows) into a display recording and into the window picker's list. | Off |
86	| **Record the camera too** | [Records a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/). | Off |
87	| **Camera** | [Which camera to record](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-camera). | The Mac's preferred camera |
88	| **Format** | [The camera's size and frame rate](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-format). | Best |
89	| The camera preview | [A live picture of the camera](/recording/record-a-camera/#check-the-picture). This row has no label, and appears only when a camera is wanted. | |
90	| **Layout** | [Where the camera lands](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) beside the screen. | Corner |
91	| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | [Runs **Clip ▸ Remove Background**](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) on the camera's clips. | Off |
92	| **Microphone** | [**Off**, or a connected microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/), with a level meter beside it. | Off |
93	| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | [Runs Enhance Voice](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the microphone's clips. | Off |
94	| **System Audio** | [Records what the Mac plays](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/). | On |
95	| **Cursor** | [Whether the pointer is drawn into the movie](/recording/cursor/): **Separate** or **In the picture**. | Separate |
96	| **Show Clicks** | [Marks each mouse click](/recording/cursor/). | Off |
97	| **Record shortcuts** | [Records the shortcuts you press](/recording/record-shortcuts/), and when you type, but never what you type. | Off |
98	| **When it lands:** **Zoom in on clicks** | [Runs Auto Zoom](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the screen clips. | On |
99	| **Show shortcuts** | [Adds shortcut overlays](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | On |
100	| **Speed up typing** | [Runs Speed Up Typing](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | Off |
101	| **Rate** | [The most frames per second](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) the file may hold, and a new project's frame rate. | 60 fps |
102	| **Size** | [Records at points or pixels](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size). | Nominal (points) |
103	| **Record Into** | [Where the recording lands](#choose-where-it-lands). | The project in front, else New Project |
104	
105	## What greys out
106	
107	Rows that don't apply to the chosen source grey out and keep their values, so nothing jumps and your settings are still there when you switch back.
108	
109	| When | Greyed out |
110	| --- | --- |
111	| **Source** is **Microphone Only** | **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout**, the background box, **System Audio**, **Cursor**, **Show Clicks**, **Record shortcuts**, the three **When it lands:** boxes and **Size**. **Rate** stays live, because it sets a new project's frame rate. |
112	| **Source** is **Camera** | The same rows, except **Camera** and **Format**, which go live. **Rate** greys out as well, because a camera records at its format's rate. |
113	| **Record the camera too** is off, with a display or window | **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and the background box. |
114	| **Microphone** is **Off** | **Enhance the microphone when it lands**. |
115	| **Record shortcuts** is off | **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. |
116	
117	**Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live for every source.
118	
119	Every control locks from the press of **Record** until the recording has landed.
120	
121	## The note under Size
122	
123	A line under **Size** tells you what you'll get from the chosen source.
124	
125	| Source | The note reads |
126	| --- | --- |
127	| A display | Both its sizes, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels` |
128	| A picked window | "the picked window's own size" |
129	| **Microphone Only** | "no picture — the microphone alone" |
130	| **Camera**, with **Format** on Best | For example `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` |
131	| **Camera**, with a format chosen | For example `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen format` |
132	| **Camera**, with none connected | "no camera connected" |
133	
134	## The footnote
135	
136	The text at the bottom left of the panel shows where recordings are saved, for example `saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`.
137	
138	When the panel stays up during a recording, as it does for a camera or a voice-over, the footnote shows the time instead: the coral **●** and the elapsed time while recording, or **❚❚** and the time held still while paused.
139	
140	## What the panel remembers
141	
142	The panel reopens as you left it, between launches. It keeps:
143	
144	- the display, the microphone, the camera and the camera format
145	- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks** and **Cursor**
146	- **Rate** and **Size**
147	- every box: **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and the three **When it lands:** boxes
148	- **Layout**
149	
150	A few things work differently:
151	
152	- **Cursor** is remembered only once you choose it. Until then it shows Separate, and a choice you make holds for every source.
153	- The camera format is one choice for every camera. A camera that doesn't have it shows Best.
154	- A picked window, and **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the **Source** row, last until you quit. The camera itself is remembered.
155	- **Record Into** isn't remembered.
156	
157	A display that's no longer connected falls back to the main display, a microphone to **Off**, and a camera to the default camera.
158	
159	## Keys in the panel
160	
161	<kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Record** and <kbd>Esc</kbd> presses **Close**.
162	
163	**Record** changes as a recording goes on, and <kbd>Return</kbd> goes with it. During the countdown <kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Cancel**, and while a camera or a voice-over records it presses **Stop**. <kbd>Esc</kbd> always closes the panel, which ends a countdown but leaves a running recording going.
164	
165	Opened with Frame Job active, the panel takes the keyboard. Opened while another app is in front, it leaves the keyboard with that app, so <kbd>Return</kbd> goes there.
166	
167	## How the panel floats
168	
169	The panel is built to sit beside whatever you're about to record.
170	
171	- It stays above other windows, and it doesn't hide when you switch to another app.
172	- Clicking it doesn't make Frame Job the active app, so your project windows don't jump over the app you're recording.
173	- Opened while Frame Job is in the background, it comes to the front without taking the keyboard, so your typing stays where it was.
174	- It opens in the centre of the screen. Drag it anywhere, and it stays there until you quit.
175	- It pushes itself back onto its display when the countdown or a note makes it taller. That way **Cancel** never ends up under the Dock. Its top-left corner stays put unless the screen edge forces a move.
176	
177	For a display or a window, the panel [leaves the screen](/recording/record-a-display/#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record) once the recording starts.
178	
179	## With an agent
180	
181	An agent doesn't use the panel. `record_screen` records for a set time, from 1 to 600 seconds, with no panel and no countdown, and returns once the recording has landed.
182	
183	- The recording lands at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, nest included, or on a new track in front when that one has no room. With no project open, it opens as a new untitled project.
184	- The tool never asks for a permission and never opens the window picker. If a permission is missing, the call stops with a message naming it and the System Settings pane to go to, so grant it once from the panel. A Frame Job launched from a terminal runs under the terminal's permissions.
185	- The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call it.
186	
187	[Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/) has every argument, and [the order its checks run in](/mcp/record-screen/#whats-checked-first).
188

215	## Record a display
216	
217	<Steps>
218	
219	1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.
220	
221	2. Choose the display by name in **Source**. There's one row for each connected display, and the panel starts on the display you used last, or the main display.
222	
223	3. Set [**Size**](#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](#choose-a-frame-rate), and anything else you want, such as the [microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
224	
225	4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown recording starts and the panel [leaves the screen](#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record). The first time, macOS asks for the Screen Recording permission instead, and you relaunch Frame Job after turning it on. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/#screen-recording).
226	
227	5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.
228	
229	</Steps>
230	
231	The recording lands in the project you chose in **Record Into**. See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/).
232	
233	## Choose a size
234	
235	**Size** sets how many pixels the movie holds.
236	
237	| Size | What you get |
238	| --- | --- |
239	| **Nominal (points)** | The display's point size. This is the default. |
240	| **Best (pixels)** | Every pixel: the point size times the display's scale, which is twice the points on a Retina display. |
241	
242	The note under the row shows both for the chosen display, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels`.
243	
244	Choose **Best (pixels)** when small text has to stay sharp, and **Nominal (points)** for a smaller picture. An odd width or height is rounded up to an even number when the movie is encoded.
245	
246	## Choose a frame rate
247	
248	**Rate** is **30 fps** or **60 fps**, and starts on 60 fps. It does two things:
249	
250	- It's the most frames per second the file may hold.
251	- It's the frame rate of a new project made from the recording.
252	
253	It's a ceiling, not a promise. macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, fractional frame rate. That's the file doing its job and not a fault.
254	
255	**Rate** greys out for **Camera**, which records at its format's rate. It stays live for **Microphone Only**, where it sets a new project's frame rate.
256	
257	## Include Frame Job windows
258	
259	Frame Job's own windows, such as the editor and the preview, are left out of a display recording. Tick **Include Frame Job windows** to put them in the picture, for example when you're recording a Frame Job tutorial. It's off by default.
260	
261	- The recorder panel is never in the picture, even with the box ticked.
262	- Frame Job's own sound stays out either way, so you can play the timeline during a recording and it won't end up in the file.
263	- The box also decides whether Frame Job's windows appear in the [window picker](/recording/record-a-window/#which-windows-the-picker-lists).
264	
265	## Where the panel goes while you record
266	
267	The panel leaves the screen once a display or window recording starts, and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) becomes your controls.
268	
269	While the panel is away, <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> stops the recording rather than showing the panel, and the Welcome window's **New Recording…** button beeps.
270	
271	After the recording lands, the panel comes back only if it was up when the recording began and there's a note to show you, such as a problem with the microphone. Otherwise it stays away until you open it again.
272	
273	The panel stays up for **Camera** and **Microphone Only**, which film nothing on screen.
274	
275	## With an agent
276	
277	An agent picks a display by number, with 0, the main display, as the default, and it can't name a display and a window at once. It sets the rest with `size` (`nominal` or `best`), `rate` (30 or 60) and `include_framejob_windows`, which is off by default. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).
278

305	## Record a window
306	
307	<Steps>
308	
309	1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.
310	
311	2. Choose **Window…** in **Source**. macOS's window picker opens.
312	
313	3. Click the window you want. **Source** now reads **Window (picked)**, and the note under **Size** reads "the picked window's own size".
314	
315	4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown recording starts and the panel leaves the screen. The first time, macOS asks for the Screen Recording permission instead, and you relaunch Frame Job after turning it on. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/#screen-recording).
316	
317	5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.
318	
319	</Steps>
320	
321	[**Size**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) work as they do for a display: **Nominal (points)** records the window at its point size, and **Best (pixels)** at every pixel.
322	
323	If the window closes while you're recording, see [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).
324	
325	## Pick a different window
326	
327	Choose **Window (picked)** again to open the picker and pick another window.
328	
329	Choosing any other row in **Source** drops the pick. A pick lasts until you quit: close and reopen the panel and it's still there, but it's never remembered between launches.
330	
331	## If you cancel the picker
332	
333	Cancel the picker and **Source** goes back to the display you used last, or the main display. That's also true when you've already picked a window and choose the row again, so the earlier pick is gone.
334	
335	If the picker can't open at all, **Source** goes back the same way and the panel reads "The window picker could not open: …" with the reason.
336	
337	## Which windows the picker lists
338	
339	The picker lists other apps' windows. Frame Job's own windows depend on **Include Frame Job windows**:
340	
341	| Box | The picker lists |
342	| --- | --- |
343	| Off | None of Frame Job's windows |
344	| On | Frame Job's windows, but never the recorder panel |
345	
346	The box only changes the next time the picker opens. A window you've already picked stays picked.
347	
348	## Record needs a picked window
349	
350	If you press **Record** while the row still reads **Window…**, with nothing picked, the panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display." No countdown starts, so nothing wrong gets recorded.
351	
352	## With an agent
353	
354	An agent doesn't use the picker. It names a window by its system window id, and if Frame Job can't record that window the call stops with an error. It can't name a window and a display at once, and `include_framejob_windows` changes nothing for a window. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).
355

368	
369	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
370	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
371	
372	Record a camera on its own when you want a piece to camera with no screen in it. Frame Job records the chosen camera at the chosen format's highest frame rate.
373	
374	<AtAGlance
375	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
376	  keys="⌥⌘N"
377	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Camera"
378	  tools="record_screen"
379	  needs="The Camera permission, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone. Screen Recording isn't needed."
380	/>
381	
382	## Record a camera on its own
383	
384	<Steps>
385	
386	1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> and choose **Camera** in **Source**.
387	
388	2. Choose the camera in [**Camera**](#choose-a-camera) and its size and frame rate in [**Format**](#choose-a-format).
389	
390	3. Check the live picture in the [preview](#check-the-picture) under **Format**.
391	
392	4. Choose a microphone in **Microphone**, or leave it **Off** to record the camera alone. The microphone can be the camera's own, if macOS lists it, and it's recorded to its own file beside the movie.
393	
394	5. Choose where it goes in **Record Into**.
395	
396	6. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown recording starts, and the panel [stays up](#stop-and-pause-from-the-panel). The first time, macOS asks for the Camera permission, and for Microphone if you chose one. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
397	
398	7. Press **Stop** in the panel when you're done.
399	
400	</Steps>
401	
402	With no camera connected, pressing **Record** says "No camera is connected."
403	
404	**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Rate** and the other rows for the screen grey out, and keep their values for next time. **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live.
405	
406	To record a camera and the screen at once, see [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).
407	
408	## Choose a camera
409	
410	**Camera** lists each connected camera by name, or a single row, **None connected**, when there isn't one. An iPhone used as a Continuity Camera has "(Continuity Camera)" after its name.
411	
412	It starts on the camera you used last, then the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected.
413	
414	The row is live when **Source** is **Camera**, or a display or window has **Record the camera too** ticked, and greyed out otherwise.
415	
416	## Choose a format
417	
418	**Format** sets the size and frame rate the camera records at.
419	
420	**Best** comes first and names what it will pick, for example **Best (1760×1328 at 30 fps)**. The camera's other formats follow, written like **1920×1080 at 30 fps**. Sizes wider than tall come first, then square, then taller than wide, each largest first.
421	
422	Each format records at its highest frame rate, so you can't choose a lower rate within a format's range.
423	
424	It starts on the format you used last when the chosen camera has it, otherwise **Best**. The row is live and greyed out at the same times as **Camera**.
425	
426	## What Best picks
427	
428	**Best** is the largest format wider than tall that reaches 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate. If two formats have the same area, the higher rate wins, and then the one the camera lists first.
429	
430	If no format wider than tall reaches 30 fps, Frame Job looks at every shape the same way. If none of those does either, it uses the format the camera is already set to.
431	
432	## Check the picture
433	
434	The preview under **Format** shows the chosen camera live at the chosen format, as the movie will record it. It isn't mirrored, so you see what's being filmed, and the whole picture is fitted inside it.
435	
436	It appears only when **Source** is **Camera**, or a display or window has **Record the camera too** ticked, and it stays live through the countdown and the recording.
437	
438	Sometimes it shows words instead of a picture.
439	
440	| The preview reads | What it means |
441	| --- | --- |
442	| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
443	| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | Frame Job doesn't have the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does. |
444	| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording the camera. The picture comes back when it's done. |
445	| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. To try again, choose another source and then **Camera**, or close and reopen the panel. |
446	
447	## How the camera warms up
448	
449	Once Frame Job has the Camera permission, the camera starts as soon as the panel shows it, so it's ready before you record, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing another source turns it off, unless it's a display or window with **Record the camera too** ticked, and so does closing the panel.
450	
451	A camera that's starting cold can take a moment to run at its full rate. Frame Job gives it up to a second before recording begins, so the recording starts steady, and then holds the camera to the chosen format and rate for the whole recording.
452	
453	If it never settles, the recording begins anyway, and the note when it lands names the rate it ran at, for example "The camera ran at 24.3 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway." If no steady frames came at all, it says that instead.
454	
455	## Stop and pause from the panel
456	
457	The panel stays on screen while a camera records, because nothing on screen is being filmed.
458	
459	- The controls lock and the microphone's level meter stays live.
460	- The [footnote](/recording/recorder-panel/#the-footnote) shows **●** or **❚❚** with the time.
461	- **Record** reads **Stop**, with a **Pause** or **Resume** button beside it.
462	
463	Choose **Close** and the panel goes away, but the recording carries on under the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/). See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) for the other ways to stop.
464	
465	## Where a camera recording lands
466	
467	The movie is saved as `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, with any microphone in its own `.m4a` file beside it.
468	
469	In an open project, the movie lands at the playhead on the front track if it fits, otherwise on a new track in front. The microphone lands on a new back track named **Microphone**.
470	
471	As a new project, the canvas takes the movie's size and the format's frame rate, rounded to a whole number.
472	
473	See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) for the full rules, and [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/) for a camera that's unplugged mid-take.
474	
475	## With an agent
476	
477	An agent picks a camera by its name or id, and a format as `1920x1080@30`, `1920x1080` for that size's highest rate, or `best`. If the camera or format isn't there, the call stops with a list of what is. `rate` and the other screen settings can't be used with a camera. Its recording starts once the camera has settled, and its time counts from the camera's first frame. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).
478

488	title: "Record a camera beside the screen"
489	description: "Record your camera at the same time as a display or a window, for a talking head over a screencast, and choose how it lands."
490	---
491	
492	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
493	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
494	
495	Tick one box and Frame Job records your camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. The camera lands as an ordinary clip on a track of its own, already laid out over the screen.
496	
497	<AtAGlance
498	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
499	  keys="⌥⌘N"
500	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record the camera too', 'New Recording panel ▸ Layout', "New Recording panel ▸ Remove the camera's background when it lands"]}
501	  tools="record_screen"
502	  needs="The Screen Recording and Camera permissions, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone."
503	/>
504	
505	## Record the screen and the camera
506	
507	<Steps>
508	
509	1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to a display or **Window…**.
510	
511	2. Tick **Record the camera too**. **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and **Remove the camera's background when it lands** go live, and a live preview of the camera appears under **Format**.
512	
513	3. Choose the camera in **Camera**, and its size and frame rate in **Format**. [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) explains both lists.
514	
515	4. Choose a [layout](#choose-a-layout).
516	
517	5. Choose a **Microphone** if you want your voice. The camera's movie has no sound of its own.
518	
519	6. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks its permissions, then counts down from 3.
520	
521	7. The panel leaves the screen. Pause and stop from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.
522	
523	</Steps>
524	
525	**Record the camera too** is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it between launches. It's live only with a display or **Window…** as the source. **Camera** and **Microphone Only** grey it out, keeping its value.
526	
527	**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen, and the note under **Size** describes the screen. The camera records at the frame rate of its **Format**.
528	
529	### What Record checks
530	
531	Pressing **Record** stops at the first thing missing, in this order:
532	
533	1. A window, when **Source** reads **Window…** with none picked. The panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display."
534	2. A camera. With none connected, the panel says "No camera is connected."
535	3. The Screen Recording permission.
536	4. The Input Monitoring permission, only with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) ticked.
537	5. The Camera permission.
538	6. The Microphone permission, only with a microphone chosen.
539	
540	[Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) says what each one asks of you.
541	
542	### The preview
543	
544	The camera starts as soon as you tick the box, so it has usually settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only** or closing the panel turns it off.
545	
546	The preview shows the chosen camera at the chosen format. When it can't, it says why:
547	
548	| The preview says | What it means |
549	| --- | --- |
550	| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
551	| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | You haven't allowed the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does, or opens System Settings if you've turned it down. |
552	| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording a camera right now. The picture comes back when it ends. |
553	| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. Untick and tick the box, or reopen the panel, to try again. |
554	
555	## Choose a layout
556	
557	**Layout** sets how the camera sits with the screen when the recording lands.
558	
559	| Layout | What it does |
560	| --- | --- |
561	| **Corner** | The default. The camera sits in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of [**View ▸ Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/). |
562	| **Rounded Corner** | The same corner with rounded edges. |
563	| **Circle** | The same corner as a circle. |
564	| **Side by Side** | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
565	| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |
566	
567	**Layout** is live only with **Record the camera too** ticked. Otherwise, and while a recording is under way, it's greyed out and keeps its value. Frame Job remembers it between launches.
568	
569	The panel offers no other corner, and no **Stacked** or **Screen Only**. [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) has those once the clip has landed. Neither offers a scale or an inset. Any crop the panel's layout makes centres on the camera's picture, not on the person.
570	
571	## The Camera track
572	
573	When the recording lands, each stretch's camera movie goes on one new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, lined up with that stretch's screen clip. A recording you never paused has one stretch. A paused one has [several](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches).
574	
575	Frame Job measures how far apart the camera and the screen started, for each stretch. The camera usually starts a moment first, so the clip's first frames are trimmed off rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.
576	
577	The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen:
578	
579	| Recording into | The undo step |
580	| --- | --- |
581	| An open project | **Add Recording**, for the screen, the camera and any microphone |
582	| A new project, one stretch | **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone. The screen movie is the project itself. |
583	| A new project, several stretches | **Add Recording Segments** |
584	
585	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the rest of the landing. Each camera file is named after its screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, for example `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`.
586	
587	## How far the layout reaches
588	
589	The layout is one layout switch at the camera clip's first frame, the same kind **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** makes, so the screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives. It ends with that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, whichever is later.
590	
591	That keeps it to this recording. A clip that was already in the project never moves, and another stretch's screen with no camera of its own stays full.
592	
593	If a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead, whichever layout you chose.
594	
595	## Remove the camera's background
596	
597	Tick **Remove the camera's background when it lands** and Frame Job runs [**Clip ▸ Remove Background**](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera's clips as soon as they land. It works on your Mac, with no key.
598	
599	The box is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it. It's greyed out, keeping its value, whenever **Layout** is.
600	
601	It's its own undo step, **Remove Background**, after the landing's and before any [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/) and the **When it lands:** boxes. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes it off and keeps the recording. If no camera clip landed, it does nothing and says nothing.
602	
603	## Change a camera clip afterwards
604	
605	Each camera clip stays an ordinary clip. You can move it, or give it another layout from [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) or the [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/).
606	
607	## Good to know
608	
609	- If the camera stops on its own during the recording, for example because it's unplugged, the screen keeps recording. What the camera wrote lands, later stretches have no camera, and the panel's note gives the reason. If it stops while the recording is starting, the recording doesn't start.
610	- A camera file that would keep less than a frame after its trim stays in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) without a clip, and a note says so. If no camera clip can be placed, no **Camera** track is added.
611	- If a stretch is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added to the project.
612	
613	## With an agent
614	
615	`record_screen` makes the same recording when it names a camera, and it can choose any of the five layouts and remove the camera's background. If no camera clip landed, the agent is told so. Landing in an open project, an agent can also leave the recording's files in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with no clips, which the panel doesn't offer. In that case no **Camera** track is added, and it can't ask for a layout or a removed background. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen).
616

632	
633	A voice-over is the microphone alone, with no picture. Use it to record narration over your edit: it lands at the playhead, on a new track of its own.
634	
635	<AtAGlance
636	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
637	  keys="⌥⌘N"

642	
643	## Record a voice-over
644	
645	<Steps>
646	
647	1. Move the playhead to where the narration should start.
648	
649	2. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to **Microphone Only**.
650	
651	3. Choose your microphone in **Microphone**.
652	
653	4. Check **Record Into**: the project to land in, or **New Project**.
654	
655	5. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the Microphone permission, then counts down from 3.
656	
657	6. Speak. The panel stays up while you do.
658	
659	7. Press **Stop**. The button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**, and the voice-over lands. The panel stays up, back on **Record**, ready for another take.
660	
661	</Steps>
662	
663	With **Microphone** set to **Off**, **Record** starts nothing and the panel says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
664	
665	The controls that only make sense for a picture grey out, keeping their values for next time: **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Cursor**, **Record shortcuts** and the **When it lands:** boxes. The note under **Size** reads "no picture — the microphone alone". **Rate** stays live, because it sets the frame rate of a new project.
666	
667	Frame Job keeps **Microphone Only** in **Source** until you quit, then goes back to your display.
668	
669	## While it records
670	
671	Nothing on screen is being filmed, so the panel stays up:
672	
673	- Its rows are locked.
674	- The [level meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) stays live.
675	- The footnote at the bottom left shows ● and the elapsed time, or ❚❚ and the time held still while paused.
676	- **Record** reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** button stands beside it, reading **Resume** while paused.
677	
678	The countdown and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) work as they do for a screen recording, so you can also pause and stop from the menu bar, or from **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>).
679	
680	**Close** takes the panel away and the voice-over carries on. To bring the panel back, click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> won't do it, because it stops the recording.
681	
682	## Where a voice-over lands
683	
684	**In an open project,** each [stretch](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) between pauses is its own file, and they land end to end from the playhead on one new track at the back, named **Microphone**. It's all one undo step, **Add Recording**. If a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) is open, they land inside it.
685	
686	A voice-over always gets a new track. It never goes on an existing one, even one already named **Microphone**.
687	
688	**As a new project,** the first file is the project itself, audio only at 1920×1080 and the frame rate in **Rate**. Later files follow it on its one track, as one undo step named **Add Recording Segments**.
689	
690	Either way they're ordinary audio clips, with everything in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/).
691	
692	## The files
693	
694	Each stretch is an `.m4a` file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by the moment it began, for example `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/).
695	
696	## Good to know
697	
698	- If the microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, and the note reads "The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped."
699	- A file too short to fill one frame stays in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) without a clip, and a note says so. If that's every file, no **Microphone** track is added.
700	- A project already at its track limit can't take the new track. The files stay on disk and the note names them. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).
701	
702	## With an agent
703	
704	`record_screen` records a voice-over too. An agent gets your Mac's default microphone rather than a chosen one, and there's no countdown. Of the screen settings, it can pass only `rate`, which sets a new project's frame rate. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

737	## Record what your Mac plays
738	
739	**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.
740	
741	With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.
742	
743	## Play the timeline while you record
744	
745	Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.
746	
747	## Record your voice
748	
749	Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.
750	
751	It works with every source. With a picture, the voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a microphone chosen, pressing **Record** also checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/).
752	
753	To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
754	
755	## Check your level
756	
757	A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.
758	
759	It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.
760	
761	## Your first words are kept
762	
763	The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.
764	
765	## How the microphone lands
766	
767	Each file lands on one new track at the back, named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.
768	
769	Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.
770	
771	If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or right after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.
772	
773	If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.
774	
775	## If the microphone stops
776	
777	A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." That stretch's microphone file isn't added to the project. It stays on disk, and the note names it when the recording lands.
778	
779	A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.
780	
781	## Plug devices in and take them out
782	
783	The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.
784	
785	- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
786	- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
787	- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
788	- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
789	- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten. The one exception is **None connected**, which leaves the remembered camera alone.
790	- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.
791	
792	## With an agent
793	
794	An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. A microphone that fails doesn't fail an agent's recording, and the result says why. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#sound).
795

18	## Start a recording
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Set up the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) and press **Record**.
23	
24	2. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) it needs.
25	
26	3. The panel counts 3, 2, 1, a second each. **Record** reads **Cancel** meanwhile, and the [microphone meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) already moves. Press **Cancel** or close the panel to stop, and nothing is recorded.
27	
28	4. The recording starts. For a display or a window, the panel leaves the screen and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) takes over. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, nothing on screen is filmed, so the panel stays up.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	## What the button says
33	
34	The panel's main button tells you where the recording has got to.
35	
36	| The button reads | What's happening | Pressing it |
37	| --- | --- | --- |
38	| **Record** | Nothing yet. | Starts the permission checks and the countdown. |
39	| **Cancel** | The countdown is running. | Ends it with nothing recorded. |
40	| **Starting…** | The recording is starting. | It's dimmed. |
41	| **Stop** | A recording runs or is paused. | Stops it and adds it to the project. |
42	| **Stopping…** | The files are being written. | It's dimmed. |
43	| **Adding…** | The files are being added to the project. | It's dimmed. |
44	
45	## If a recording doesn't start
46	
47	A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails rather than hanging. The panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to **Record**. Any other failed start puts its reason in the same note.
48	
49	While the button reads **Starting…**, you can still stop with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>, or by closing the panel. The **File** item may still read **New Recording…** at that moment. If Frame Job hadn't begun yet, the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded." A moment later, it's too late to abandon: the recording ends as soon as it begins, and whatever it caught lands as usual.
50	
51	## One recording at a time
52	
53	Only one recording runs at a time. If you press **Record** while another runs or is paused, including one an agent started, the countdown runs and the panel then says "A recording is already in progress."
54	
55	## Pause and resume
56	
57	You can pause from any of these:
58	
59	- the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)'s **Pause Recording**
60	- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under **New Recording…**
61	- the panel's **Pause** button, for a [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) or a [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
62	
63	While paused, each of these reads **Resume Recording** or **Resume**. The **File** item is available only while a recording runs or is paused. Pausing has no keyboard shortcut.
64	
65	If Frame Job can't pause a recording you started, it beeps and the recording carries on. A resume that fails leaves it paused, with the reason in the panel's note: at once if the panel is up, otherwise when it comes back after you stop. Try again, or stop and land what you have.
66	
67	## Paused recordings are stretches
68	
69	A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several stretches. Each stretch has its own movie, and its own microphone, camera and [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) when the recording has them.
70	
71	- Each file is named by the moment its stretch began.
72	- Each stretch keeps its own width, height and frame rate.
73	- The paused time is in no file, and the elapsed time counts only what was recorded.
74	
75	When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone goes on the **Microphone** track, lined up with its own picture.
76	
77	## Stop a recording
78	
79	You can stop a running or paused recording from any of these:
80	
81	- the menu-bar item's **Stop Recording**
82	- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>). While any recording runs, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording**, paused included.
83	- the panel's **Stop** button, for a camera on its own or a voice-over
84	
85	Frame Job writes the files and [adds the recording to your project](/recording/where-it-lands/). If it lands with nothing to report, a hidden panel [stays hidden](/recording/where-it-lands/#when-the-panel-comes-back). Press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> when you want it again.
86	
87	:::caution
88	There's no global shortcut to stop. <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> works in Frame Job's own menus, so it does nothing while another app is in front. Use the menu-bar item.
89	:::
90	
91	## Stop from macOS's indicator
92	
93	macOS shows its own indicator in the menu bar during a screen recording, and it can end the recording too. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it. The panel's note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added." An agent's result says it was stopped this way.
94	
95	## The Welcome window during a recording
96	
97	The **New Recording…** button on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) never stops a recording.
98	
99	- During a screen recording you started in the panel, it only beeps. Use **File ▸ Stop Recording** or the menu-bar item.
100	- During a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
101	
102	## If the panel closes
103	
104	A recording carries on if the panel closes, under the menu-bar item and **File ▸ Stop Recording**. You can only do this with a camera on its own or a voice-over, because the panel is off screen for anything else.
105	
106	Closing it at other moments is different:
107	
108	- During the countdown, it cancels the countdown and nothing is recorded.
109	- While the button reads **Starting…**, it counts as a Stop.
110	- Closing also lets go of a microphone or camera that was warming up for a recording.
111	
112	## Quit during a recording
113	
114	Choosing **Quit Frame Job** (<kbd>⌘Q</kbd>) during a recording doesn't quit. It puts the recording's controls in front of you, so you can stop or resume first:
115	
116	- With the panel hidden for a screen recording, it opens the menu-bar item's menu.
117	- For a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
118	
119	Frame Job reviews your unsaved projects before this. If that review closes the project you were recording into, the recording opens as a new project when it lands, and the note says so.
120	
121	## Stop an agent's recording
122	
123	A recording an agent starts shows the same menu-bar item, so you can pause, resume or stop it from there or from the **File** menu.
124	
125	Your Stop ends the agent's recording early, and what was recorded still lands. The agent's result shows the shorter length, and lists each stretch with the number of pauses. An agent asks for a length of real time, so a pause shortens what gets recorded rather than extending it. An agent has no way to pause or resume, and it has no countdown. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it).

147	## What it shows
148	
149	The item appears when the recording starts, and shows the elapsed time as `m:ss`, then `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Hover over it and its tooltip says which state it's in.
150	
151	| State | The menu bar shows | Tooltip | Its menu |
152	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
153	| Recording | A coral ● and the running time | "Frame Job is recording" | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
154	| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | "Frame Job's recording is paused" | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
155	
156	It needs no permission. It appears for an agent's recording too, so you can [pause or stop one](/recording/pause-and-stop/#stop-an-agents-recording). It comes down the moment the recording ends, before the recording has landed.
157	
158	## Pause, resume and stop
159	
160	Click the item for its menu.
161	
162	- **Pause Recording** pauses. The row then reads **Resume Recording**.
163	- **Stop Recording** stops the recording, running or paused, and adds it to your project.
164	
165	The time keeps ticking while the menu is open, so you can read it before you decide. [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) has the other places to do this. If you choose **Quit Frame Job** while the panel is hidden for a screen recording, Frame Job opens this menu instead of quitting.
166	
167	## The keyboard mark
168	
169	While a recording [records shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row. Both show whether the recording is running or paused, and they hold for a recording an agent started with shortcuts on.
170	
171	## A fixed width
172	
173	The item is sized once, so the other items in your menu bar don't shift as the seconds tick, when the hours appear, or at a pause. It's sized for times up to 9:59:59, and a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. Past 9:59:59 the label is wider than that.
174	
175	## If macOS hides the item
176	
177	macOS can drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch. **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work once you switch to Frame Job.

188	---
189	
190	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
191	
192	When you stop, Frame Job adds the recording to your work without asking anything: into the project you chose, at its playhead, or as a new project. A recording is ordinary media from then on, so you can cut, move and delete its clips like any others.
193	
194	<AtAGlance
195	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
196	  keys="⌥⌘N"
197	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Record Into"
198	  tools={['record_screen', 'undo']}
199	/>
200	
201	## Choose where it goes
202	
203	Before you press Record, set **Record Into** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). It lists **New Project** and every open project. It follows whichever project is in front until you pick a row yourself, and it's fixed once you press Record, so switching windows during a recording doesn't change where it goes.
204	
205	While the files are written and imported, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**.
206	
207	## Into an open project
208	
209	The recording goes in at the chosen project's playhead, in whatever is open there. If you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it lands inside the nest.
210	
211	| What was recorded | Where it lands |
212	| --- | --- |
213	| The picture, from a screen or a camera on its own | On the front track, when all of it fits there. Otherwise all of it goes on a new track in front of everything. |
214	| The microphone | On a new back track named **Microphone**. |
215	| A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) | On a new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, in the panel's **Layout**. |
216	| A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) | On a new back track named **Microphone**, from the playhead. |
217	
218	A recording's picture is never split across two tracks. An existing Microphone track is never reused: each recording makes its own.
219	
220	The microphone file and the movie don't start at quite the same moment, so Frame Job measures how far apart they began and places the microphone clip to match. When that would start it before the beginning of the timeline, or on top of the stretch before it, its head is trimmed instead.
221	
222	Every clip that landed is selected afterwards, microphone and camera clips included.
223	
224	## Land a paused recording
225	
226	Each [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch. They land as one clip per stretch, back to back on one track. They touch, they never overlap, and no transition joins them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.
227	
228	At an uneven project frame rate, such as 24.981 fps, a gap of less than a frame can remain between two stretches.
229	
230	## Undo a landing
231	
232	Everything that lands in an open project is one undo step, **Add Recording**. **Edit ▸ Undo Add Recording** removes the clips and their media entries and leaves the files on disk, as undoing **Add Media…** does.
233	
234	Anything set up in [When it lands](/recording/when-it-lands/) runs after the landing as its own undo steps, so those come off first.
235	
236	## As a new project
237	
238	With **Record Into** set to **New Project**, the recording opens in a new, untitled project named after its file, such as `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`. That's the name Save offers.
239	
240	The canvas takes the movie's size and the frame rate you chose in **Rate**, while the media keeps the file's own frame rate. Two sources differ:
241	
242	- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) sets the canvas to the file's size at the camera format's frame rate.
243	- A voice-over has no picture, so the canvas is 1920×1080 at **Rate**, and later stretches follow the first on its one track.
244	
245	The project is unsaved, and it asks before it closes.
246	
247	The first stretch's picture is the project itself, so it has no undo step. Everything else that landed with it is one step, named for what it holds:
248	
249	| What landed beside the first picture | Undo step |
250	| --- | --- |
251	| A microphone | **Add Microphone** |
252	| A camera | **Add Camera** |
253	| A camera and a microphone | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
254	| Later stretches, with or without a microphone or camera | **Add Recording Segments** |
255	| Only [click ripples](/recording/cursor/#show-clicks) | **Cursor Clicks** |
256	| Nothing | No step |
257	
258	Undoing that step keeps the first picture, leaves the files on disk, and leaves the project unsaved.
259	
260	## If you're dragging when it ends
261	
262	If you're in the middle of a drag in the chosen project when the recording ends, the landing waits for the drag to finish, for up to 20 seconds. After that it gives up, and the panel's note reads "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: A drag was still in progress after 20 s." The files are on disk either way, and you can bring them in with [**Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/).
263	
264	## If the chosen project closed
265	
266	If the project you chose closes while you're recording, the recording opens as a new project instead, and the panel's note says "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
267	
268	## When the panel comes back
269	
270	A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Once it has landed, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it. While a recording runs, the same keys stop it.
271	
272	The panel returns on its own, with a note, only if it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to report. The note can hold several of these at once.
273	
274	| The note says | What happened |
275	| --- | --- |
276	| "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added." | You stopped it from macOS's own indicator, not from Frame Job. |
277	| "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added." | The display slept or went away. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/). |
278	| "The camera stopped on its own. What was captured was added." | A camera recording ended because the camera stopped. The first sentence can give the camera's own reason instead. |
279	| "A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …" | One stretch's movie couldn't be read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume. The other stretches landed. |
280	| "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture." | That stretch's microphone file was readable, so it's on the Microphone track where the picture would have been. The next picture starts after that gap. |
281	| A sentence about the microphone | It stopped or failed. The picture still landed. |
282	| A sentence about a [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) | It stopped or failed. The screen recording still landed. |
283	| "The camera ran at … fps, not its …, in the … s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway." | The camera didn't reach its format's frame rate before the recording began. "The camera delivered no steady frames…" is the same note when it sent none. |
284	| A sentence about resuming | Resuming after a [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) failed, and the sentence says why. |
285	| "… is too short for a frame (… ms) and was added to the media list without a clip." | The file is in the Media tab, with nothing on the timeline. |
286	| "… was added to the media list without a clip: …" | The file couldn't be placed, and the sentence says why. |
287	| "The cursor file for … was not written: …" | That stretch has no [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). |
288	| "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." | The files didn't close within 10 seconds of the stop. The note names the files kept on disk. |
289	| "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …" | Nothing landed. The note names every file, which are all on disk. |
290	
291	## Good to know
292	
293	- A project already at its limit of 64 tracks can't take a recording that needs a new track. The picture and the microphone land together or not at all, so if the picture would fit and the microphone wouldn't, nothing lands. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
294	- A recording fails outright only when no movie could be read at all, or when the capture failed while the movie was being written. Its note names every file on disk.
295	- When a stretch is left out, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its kept files, but it isn't added to the project.
296	- In a new project, a left-out first stretch's microphone goes to the Media tab with no clip, because the first readable picture starts the project at 0.
297	
298	## With an agent
299	
300	`record_screen` lands a recording the same way, with two differences:
301	
302	- With no project open, it always opens a new project. Whenever a recording opens as a new project, including when the chosen project closed, the answer says `landed: new_project`, and later calls reach that project with `project` set to the recording's path.
303	- With `place: false` it adds the recording to the Media tab with no clip, which the panel can't, and the note says to place it with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_clip). A new project's picture is on the timeline whatever `place` says. `camera_layout` and the [steps after landing](/recording/when-it-lands/#with-an-agent) can't be used with it.
304	
305	See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

334	  alt="The New Recording panel. Under the Layout row, Remove the camera's background when it lands is greyed out. Under Microphone, Enhance the microphone when it lands is greyed out. Under When it lands, Zoom in on clicks is ticked, Show shortcuts is ticked and greyed out, and Speed up typing is unticked and greyed out."
335	/>
336	
337	## Choose what runs
338	
339	Tick the boxes on the panel before you press Record.
340	
341	| Box | Runs | On | Default | Available when |
342	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
343	| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | The camera's clips | Off | **Record the camera too** is ticked beside a display or a window |
344	| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** | The microphone's clips | Off | A microphone is chosen, on any source |
345	| **Zoom in on clicks** | **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | The screen clips | On | The source is a display or a window |
346	| **Show shortcuts** | **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** | The screen clips | On | The source is a display or a window, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |
347	| **Speed up typing** | **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The screen clips | Off | The source is a display or a window, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |
348	
349	A greyed box keeps its value for next time, and every box is greyed while a recording is under way. The panel remembers all five between uses.
350	
351	The screen clips are the clips of each stretch's movie that has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). No other clip is touched, and a voice-over or a camera on its own has none.
352	
353	:::note
354	**Zoom in on clicks** is on from the start, so a display or window recording lands with zooms unless you untick it. **Show shortcuts** is on too, but it does nothing until you tick [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), which is off.
355	:::
356	
357	## The order they run in
358	
359	The steps always run in this order, whichever you tick:
360	
361	1. **Remove Background**, straight after the landing.
362	2. **Enhance Voice**, once the sound has been analysed.
363	3. **Auto Zoom**.
364	4. **Add Shortcut Overlays**.
365	5. **Speed Up Typing**, once the speech has been detected.
366	
367	Each is its own undo step, named as in this list, and they all come after the landing's. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes them off one at a time, last first, and keeps the recording.
368	
369	The order matters. Zooms are planned on whole clips before the speed-up splits them, and the speed-up leaves each overlay at its pace.
370	
371	Each command uses the settings its own menu command would, and only Enhance Voice shows a sheet. Nothing asks you a question.
372	
373	## Remove the camera's background
374	
375	**Remove the camera's background when it lands** runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera's clips straight after the landing, with nothing to wait for. If no camera clip landed, it does nothing and says nothing. [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/#remove-the-cameras-background) has the rest.
376	
377	## Enhance the microphone
378	
379	**Enhance the microphone when it lands** runs [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) on each stretch's microphone file, or on a voice-over's files. It never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.
380	
381	Enhance Voice needs the sound's loudness and speech analysed first, so it waits for that after the files land. It then runs under the **Measuring Sound** sheet, at the target loudness of the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, and its settings appear in the clip's [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
382	
383	Choosing **Cancel** on the sheet leaves the clips as they landed.
384	
385	**Edit ▸ Undo Enhance Voice** takes the processing off and keeps the recording. The next undo is **Remove Background** if that ran, then the landing's own step: **Add Recording** in an open project, and in a new project a step such as **Add Microphone**, or nothing when the recording is a single file.
386	
387	If a second recording lands in the same project while the first is still waiting, its clips join the wait and the wait starts again.
388	
389	## Zoom in on clicks
390	
391	**Zoom in on clicks** runs [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) with the values the Auto Zoom sheet last used. **Zoom on typing** is turned on when the recording has typing, and off when it hasn't.
392	
393	## Show shortcuts
394	
395	**Show shortcuts** runs [Add Shortcut Overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) with its usual settings: at the bottom of the picture, in the dark theme.
396	
397	## Speed up typing
398	
399	**Speed up typing** runs [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) with the values its sheet last used. It waits until the speech has been detected, so typing you talk over keeps its pace.
400	
401	A speed-up that would leave a clip silent above ×12 is never applied here, because the panel can't ask you first. The foot of the inspector says so instead. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** yourself to be asked. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
402	
403	## What the steps wait for
404	
405	Enhance Voice, Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing each hold off while:
406	
407	- you're dragging in the project
408	- a sheet is up on its window
409	- you're inside a different nest from the one the recording landed in
410	
411	They carry on by themselves once that's over. Each waits for up to 5 minutes. The clock starts at the landing or when the step before it ran. For the first step after Enhance Voice, it starts when Enhance Voice stops waiting.
412	
413	## When a step can't run
414	
415	A problem shows at the foot of the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/), with no beep and no sheet. A step with nothing to do says nothing at all: a recording with no cursor file, a recording with no microphone clip, or no click, shortcut or typing stretch long enough changes nothing and shows no message.
416	
417	| The inspector says | What happened | What runs next |
418	| --- | --- | --- |
419	| "Enhance Voice did not run on the recording: its microphone was not ready to measure within 5 minutes. Select its clip and choose Clip ▸ Enhance Voice." | The sound wasn't analysed in time, or the project stayed busy. | The other steps |
420	| "Nothing could be enhanced. …" | There was nothing to measure, for example a silent microphone. The sentence gives the reason. | The other steps |
421	| "… did not run on the recording: the project was busy for 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ …" | You were dragging, a sheet was up, or you were in another nest for the whole wait. | Nothing. Run the rest yourself. |
422	| "Speed Up Typing did not run on the recording: its speech was not detected within 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…." | Speech detection didn't finish in time, or the project stayed busy. | It's the last step. |
423	| "Clip … now plays above ×12, so its audio is left out: it is silent in the preview and the export." | The speed-up would do this, so it was left off. Despite the wording, nothing changed. | It's the last step. |
424	| Any other sentence | The command wouldn't run. This is the sentence it would show from its own menu item. | The next step |
425	
426	A cursor file that can't be read is reported the same way, and none of the steps that use it runs after that.
427	
428	## With an agent
429	
430	`record_screen` can run the same steps, through its `camera_cutout`, `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` arguments, with some differences:
431	
432	- Every step is off unless the agent asks for it, **Zoom in on clicks** included.
433	- Every step needs the recording placed on the timeline, so none works with `place: false`.
434	- `enhance` needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.
435	- `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` need `keys: "shortcuts"`.
436	- `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` can't be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own.
437	- Enhance Voice runs at −16 LUFS, not at the Normalize row's target. The agent can call [`enhance_voice`](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice) afterwards for another target.
438	- The other steps use the tools' own defaults, never the values a sheet remembers.
439	- A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and the agent is told.
440	
441	The call's answer holds each step's own answer, or a sentence under `enhance_error`, `auto_zoom_error` and so on when the step couldn't run. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#run-steps-after-it-lands).
442

454	title: "Recording files and formats"
455	description: "Where recordings are saved, how their files are named, what format each one is, and why a still screen gives a low frame rate."
456	---
457	
458	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
459	
460	Every recording is a set of ordinary files in one folder, so they outlast any project they land in. This page lists what each recording writes and in what format.
461	
462	<AtAGlance
463	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
464	  keys="⌥⌘N"
465	  tools="record_screen"
466	/>
467	
468	## Where recordings are saved
469	
470	Recordings go in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, which Frame Job creates the first time it needs it. The panel's footnote shows the folder before you start.
471	
472	They're never stored inside the project package. A recording is original footage, so it survives even if you never save the project it opened in, and undoing a landing leaves its files on disk. To carry recordings into the package, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
473	
474	## What each recording writes
475	
476	| File | Example name | Format |
477	| --- | --- | --- |
478	| [Screen movie](#the-screen-movie) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
479	| [Its microphone](#the-microphone-file) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | AAC audio |
480	| [Its cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Frame Job's own |
481	| [Voice-over](#voice-over-files) | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | AAC audio |
482	| [Camera on its own](#camera-files) | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
483	| [Camera beside the screen](#camera-files) | `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
484	
485	## How files are named
486	
487	A file is named by the date and time it began, on a 24-hour clock in your Mac's time zone.
488	
489	A [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file and a resume starts a new one, so each stretch of a paused recording is its own set of files, named by the time that stretch began.
490	
491	When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
492	
493	## The screen movie
494	
495	A screen recording is a QuickTime `.mov` in HEVC where your Mac offers it, otherwise H.264. Its size comes from the panel's **Size** row, **Nominal (points)** or **Best (pixels)**, measured on the display or on a picked window's own size.
496	
497	With **System Audio** on, the movie has one stereo 48 kHz sound track of what your Mac plays. Frame Job's own sound is left out, so playing your timeline during a recording doesn't get into it.
498	
499	The microphone is never a track of the movie.
500	
501	## The microphone file
502	
503	The microphone is written beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, as an AAC `.m4a` file.
504	
505	Keeping it apart from the system sound means you can set the level of your voice and your computer's sound separately. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
506	
507	## Voice-over files
508	
509	A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) is an AAC `.m4a` named `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a`, one file for each stretch between pauses.
510	
511	## Camera files
512	
513	A camera recording is a QuickTime `.mov` at the camera's format, in HEVC where that can be used at the format's size, otherwise H.264. It has no sound of its own.
514	
515	- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) is named `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`.
516	- A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) is named after the screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, one for each stretch.
517	
518	Any microphone file sits beside the movie, named as for a screen recording.
519	
520	## Why a still screen gives a low frame rate
521	
522	macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, fractional frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The picture holds until the next change.
523	
524	**Rate**, 30 or 60 fps, is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses it as its frame rate, while the media in the project keeps the file's real rate.
525	
526	Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.
527	
528	## With an agent
529	
530	An agent can record into another folder, created if it's missing, which the panel can't. It names the folder only: the file always takes its dated name.
531	
532	The call's answer gives the files it wrote, as `path`, `mic_path` and `camera_path`. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#what-it-answers).
533	
534	## Related

538	- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
