542	title: "The cursor in a recording"
543	description: "Choose whether the pointer is kept out of a screen recording for Frame Job to draw, or drawn into the movie by macOS, and how clicks are shown."
544	---
545	
546	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
547	
548	A screen recording can keep the pointer out of the movie, so Frame Job draws it on the clip and you can restyle it later, or have macOS draw it into the picture for good. You choose before you record, because the choice is part of the movie.
549	
550	<AtAGlance
551	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
552	  keys="⌥⌘N"
553	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Cursor', 'New Recording panel ▸ Show Clicks']}
554	  tools="record_screen"
555	/>
556	
557	## Choose Separate or In the picture
558	
559	Set **Cursor** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
560	
561	| | **Separate** | **In the picture** |
562	| --- | --- | --- |
563	| The pointer | Kept out of the movie. Frame Job draws it on the clip. | Drawn into the movie by macOS. |
564	| Restyle it later | Yes, in the clip's **Cursor** section. | No. It can't be changed or removed. |
565	| **Show Clicks** | Click ripples, drawn by Frame Job. | A ring drawn into the movie. |
566	| The **Cursor** section | Appears on the clip. | Doesn't appear. |
567	| Cursor file | Written | Written |
568	
569	**Separate** is the default for every screen source: displays, windows and picked windows. Your choice is remembered, and once you've made one it holds for every source.
570	
571	Both write a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) beside the movie, so [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) work either way.
572	
573	With **Separate**, the pointer appears wherever Frame Job draws the clip, in the preview and in every export. The movie file on its own has no pointer, so opened in another app it shows none.
574	
575	**Cursor** is greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the source, and while a recording is under way.
576	
577	## Show clicks
578	
579	**Show Clicks** marks each mouse click. It's off by default, and greyed out with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**.
580	
581	- **With In the picture**, macOS draws a ring around each click into the movie. It can't be removed afterwards.
582	- **With Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie. Frame Job draws the ripples from the cursor file, and you can edit them afterwards.
583	
584	## What a Separate recording lands with
585	
586	The clip gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, with the pointer drawn as recorded. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) for what you can change there.
587	
588	With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording. In a new project where that's the only other change, the undo step is called **Cursor Clicks**. Undoing it takes the ripples off and keeps the pointer.
589	
590	Nothing else is set. To smooth the pointer's path and hide it when it's idle, choose **Polish** in the same section.
591	
592	## What an In the picture recording lands with
593	
594	The pointer is in the movie and the cursor file says so, so the clip shows no **Cursor** section and nothing is drawn twice.
595	
596	## Good to know
597	
598	If a **Separate** stretch's cursor file couldn't be written, that stretch has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. It gets no ripples either. The panel's note says so, with "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
599	
600	## With an agent
601	
602	`record_screen` takes `cursor`, either `separate` or `in_picture`, and leaving it out means `separate`. Its `show_clicks` is `false` unless the agent sets it. Neither can be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#pointer-and-keys).
603	
604	## Related
605	
606	- [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/)
607	- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
608	- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
609	- [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/)

611	title: "Style the recorded cursor"
612	description: Change how a recording's pointer looks after you've recorded it, from its size and path to when it hides and a ring on every click.
613	---
614	
615	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
616	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
617	
618	When a screen recording keeps its pointer out of the movie, Frame Job draws the pointer for you, so you can restyle it long after you stopped recording. The **Cursor** section makes it bigger, calms a shaky path, hides it when it rests and puts a ring on every click.
619	
620	<AtAGlance
621	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor"
622	  tools={['set_video', 'paste_attributes', 'get_cursor_events']}
623	  needs="A screen recording made with Cursor set to Separate, the default, so its pointer isn't in the movie."
624	/>
625	
626	## Find the Cursor section
627	
628	<Steps>
629	
630	1. Select a recording's clip on the timeline.
631	
632	2. Open the **Clip** tab's **Picture** sub-tab.
633	
634	3. Open the **Cursor** section, after **Background**. It starts shut.
635	
636	</Steps>
637	
638	The section's header sums up what's set: **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple.
639	
640	The section is there only when every selected clip comes from a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) that the picture doesn't already show:
641	
642	- A recording made with **Cursor:** set to **In the picture** has no section, because the pointer is part of the movie and would otherwise be drawn twice. See [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
643	- A movie with no cursor file has no section. If the file exists but didn't come along, [attach it with Locate…](/recording/cursor-files/#attach-or-re-point-a-cursor-file).
644	- A selection that also holds any other kind of clip has no section.
645	
646	A freeze frame of a recording has the section too, with the pointer held where it was on that frame.
647	
648	Each row is its own undo step. If the selected clips disagree about a row, it shows as mixed.
649	
650	## Tidy the pointer in one click
651	
652	Choose **Polish** at the bottom of the section. It sets **Smoothing** to **Medium** and **Hide when idle** to **3 s**, as one undo step called "Polish Cursor". Nothing else changes, and you can adjust either row afterwards.
653	
654	## The controls
655	
656	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
657	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
658	| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer. | On | On, off |
659	| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. | 100 % | 25–800 % |
660	| **Style** | Which pointer is drawn. | As recorded | As recorded, Arrow |
661	| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. | Off | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
662	| **Hide when idle** | Fades out a resting pointer. | Never | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 s |
663	| **Clicks** | Draws a ring out of every click. | None | None, Ripple |
664	| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. | White at 80 % | Any colour |
665	| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. | 100 % | 25–400 % |
666	
667	## Show or resize the pointer
668	
669	Untick **Show cursor** to draw no pointer on this clip. Click rings are separate, so with **Clicks** set to **Ripple** the rings still draw without a pointer. That's useful when you want to show where someone clicked and nothing else.
670	
671	**Size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %. Its slider runs to 400 %, and you can type up to 800 % in the field.
672	
673	## Choose the pointer's style
674	
675	**Style** offers **As recorded** and **Arrow**. Frame Job's recordings don't store pictures of the pointer, so both choices draw Frame Job's arrow, and a pointer that was an I-beam or a hand on screen is drawn as the arrow too. The only difference you'll see is that the section's header reads **arrow** rather than **on**.
676	
677	Frame Job's arrow is a black arrow with a white outline, 14 by 21 points at 100 %. It's drawn at the recording's own pixel density and redrawn for each **Size** rather than stretched, so it stays crisp.
678	
679	## Calm a shaky path
680	
681	**Smoothing** irons out the wobble in the pointer's path, from **Light** through **Medium** to **Strong**. The pointer still reaches every click exactly, at the moment of the click, and a pause stays a pause.
682	
683	## Hide a resting pointer
684	
685	**Hide when idle** fades the pointer out after the time you pick with no movement and no mouse press. Scrolling and typing don't count as activity. The fade takes 0.2 s, and the pointer comes back 0.15 s before it next moves or clicks, so it's already there when it sets off.
686	
687	## Show clicks
688	
689	Set **Clicks** to **Ripple** to draw a ring growing out of every press of a mouse button. A ring lasts 0.45 s, growing quickly at first and fading as it goes, and up to four can show at once. At 100 % it reaches 24 points from the click.
690	
691	**Ripple color** and **Ripple size** are live only while **Clicks** is **Ripple**. **Ripple size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150 and 200 %.
692	
693	**Clicks** starts at **None**, unless the recording was made with **Show Clicks:** on and **Cursor:** set to **Separate**. Those clips land with **Ripple** already set.
694	
695	## Put everything back
696	
697	**Reset** in the section's header appears once something differs from its default. It sets all eight rows back to the defaults in the table, as one undo step called "Reset Cursor".
698	
699	## Change the pointer part-way through a clip
700	
701	Select an [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip and the section edits that action instead of the whole clip:
702	
703	| Rows | With an action selected |
704	| --- | --- |
705	| **Size**, **Ripple size** | Animate across the action. |
706	| **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** | Switch at the action's end. The row says **at end**. |
707	| **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** | Always change the clip itself. Their rows show ⊘. |
708	
709	**Polish** also changes the clip itself, whatever is selected. **Reset** isn't offered while an action is selected. Once the action holds a cursor change, the section's header shows **Clear** in its place, which takes every cursor change out of that action as one undo step called "Clear". **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle** stay as they are on the clip.
710	
711	The first time you change one of the action rows on a clip with no cursor settings of its own, Frame Job stores the defaults on the clip in the same step. That's what lets **Size** and **Ripple size** animate from 100 % instead of jumping.
712	
713	## Copy the settings to another clip
714	
715	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, along with the rest of its picture settings. The settings are replaced as a whole, so pasting from a clip whose cursor you never changed puts the target's back to the defaults. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
716	
717	## Streak a moving pointer
718	
719	With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0, in the **Transform** section, a moving pointer is streaked along its path across the shutter. That happens even when the clip itself stands still. A still pointer and the click rings stay sharp.
720	
721	The streak shows in the preview, in rendered frames and in every export. A clip that [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp keeps its pointer sharp, and so does a freeze frame.
722	
723	## How the pointer sits in the picture
724	
725	The pointer is drawn inside its clip, as if it were part of the movie. So it follows the clip's zooms, placement and crop, it takes the clip's grade, and the preview, rendered frames and exports all agree. In an HLG project the pointer and its rings are lifted to match the picture.
726	
727	It also follows the clip's time. Change the clip's speed and the pointer speeds up with it. [Reverse the clip](/speed/reverse/) and the pointer plays backwards too.
728	
729	## Good to know
730	
731	- A cursor file loads in the background and never holds up the preview. Until it's ready the frame draws without the pointer, then redraws with it. Changing **Smoothing** can do the same for a moment, because the new path has to be worked out. Rendered frames and exports wait for the file.
732	- **Hide when idle** and the ring's 0.45 s count in the recording's own time, so on a clip at 2× they pass twice as fast.
733	- [Splitting](/editing/splitting/) a clip or making a freeze frame keeps the clip's own **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle**, even from inside an action.
734	- Paste onto a clip with no cursor file and the settings are kept but nothing is drawn.
735	- If a cursor file is missing or can't be read, the clip draws with no pointer. See [When a cursor file has a problem](/recording/cursor-files/#when-a-cursor-file-has-a-problem).
736	
737	## With an agent
738	
739	`set_video`'s `cursor` key sets the same eight values, and it isn't held to the pop-ups' steps. **Smoothing** can be any value from 0 to 1, where **Light** is 0.25, **Medium** 0.5 and **Strong** 1, and **Hide when idle** anything from 0.5 to 30 seconds. **Size** is a scale from 0.25 to 8 and **Ripple size** one from 0.25 to 4.
740	
741	`{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults on the clip and `cursor: null` clears them. Frame Job won't accept a value outside its range, and it doesn't round one to fit. See [the `cursor` key](/mcp/tools-set-video/#cursor) for the full list.
742	
743	To see what a recording's pointer did before styling it, an agent reads the cursor file with [`get_cursor_events`](/mcp/tools-recording/#get_cursor_events).
744

2	title: "Cursor files"
3	description: Understand the file that holds a recording's pointer, clicks and keys, how it follows its movie, and how to fix it when it doesn't.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	A cursor file sits beside a screen recording and holds what the pointer did, so Frame Job can draw and restyle the pointer later. You rarely touch one. This page is for when a movie has moved, lost its file or picked up the wrong one.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  where="Media tab ▸ Cursor"
14	  tools={['set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']}
15	/>
16	
17	## What a cursor file holds
18	
19	Every recording of a display, a window or a picked window writes a cursor file, whichever **Cursor:** option you chose. A camera on its own and a voice-over don't, because they have no pointer. The file has the movie's name, ending in `.fjcursor`, and sits in the same folder:
20	
21	```
22	Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov
23	Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor
24	```
25	
26	A paused recording has one movie per stretch between pauses, and each movie gets its own file.
27	
28	The file is plain text and records:
29	
30	- Where the pointer was, about 120 times a second.
31	- Every click and every scroll.
32	- How the recorded area sat on the screen, so a window that moved mid-recording still lines up.
33	- With [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, the shortcuts you pressed and when you typed. A typed key is stored as a time only, never as a character.
34	
35	It holds no pictures of the pointer, so the pointer you see drawn is [Frame Job's arrow](/recording/cursor-settings/#choose-the-pointers-style).
36	
37	With **Cursor:** set to **In the picture**, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well and the file says so. Frame Job then draws nothing over the clip, and the clip has no **Cursor** section. The file is still used for its clicks and keys.
38	
39	[Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/), [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) all read this file.
40	
41	## How the file follows its movie
42	
43	Frame Job keeps a movie and its cursor file together wherever it can. Keep them in the same folder with the same name when you move them by hand, and an import will find the file.
44	
45	### When a recording lands
46	
47	Each stretch's movie gets its own cursor file attached as it lands. You don't need to do anything.
48	
49	### When you import a movie
50	
51	When you import a movie, whether with **File ▸ Add Media…**, by dropping it on the window or by opening it, Frame Job looks beside the movie for a file with the same name ending in `.fjcursor`. It takes that file only if it reads as a cursor file and was made for a movie of exactly this size.
52	
53	A file that's missing, damaged or made for another size is left alone and the movie imports without it. Frame Job says nothing about it, so if a recording arrives with no **Cursor** section, check the [Media tab](#see-a-movies-cursor-file).
54	
55	A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a movie as it imports, and that copy isn't looked beside.
56	
57	### When you relink a movie
58	
59	[Relinking](/projects/relink-media/) takes the cursor file beside the new movie. If there's none, the media keeps the cursor file it already had, as long as that file is still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file after the relink, and you can attach one with **Locate…**.
60	
61	### When you consolidate
62	
63	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies each cursor file into the package beside its movie, and a moved package finds it there again when you open it.
64	
65	If a cursor file is missing, Consolidate leaves it alone and its report says so, for example "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." If a copy fails, the media goes on pointing at the original file. A movie that's missing is left alone along with its cursor file.
66	
67	## See a movie's cursor file
68	
69	Select a video in the **Media** tab's list and read its **Cursor** section. The section appears once the project has a video with a picture.
70	
71	<Shot
72	  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
73	  alt="The Media tab with three files in its list and nothing selected. Below the list, the Camera Log section reads Select a video in the list, and the Cursor section at the bottom has a File row with dimmed Locate… and Remove buttons."
74	/>
75	
76	| The section says | What it means |
77	| --- | --- |
78	| "Select a video in the list" | Nothing that can carry a cursor file is selected. |
79	| "No cursor file" | This video has none attached. |
80	| The file's name | The file is attached and on disk. |
81	| The file's name, then "— missing" | The file is attached but has gone from where it was. |
82	
83	## Attach or re-point a cursor file
84	
85	Use **Locate…** to give a video its cursor file, or to point it at one that has moved.
86	
87	<Steps>
88	
89	1. Select the video in the **Media** tab's list.
90	
91	2. In the **Cursor** section, choose **Locate…**.
92	
93	3. Choose the `.fjcursor` file recorded with this movie.
94	
95	</Steps>
96	
97	Frame Job runs the same check as an import: the file must read as a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size. If it passes, that's one undo step called "Locate Cursor File". If it doesn't, an alert titled "The cursor file was not attached" gives the reason and nothing changes. For example:
98	
99	- "The cursor file *name* was not attached: its movie_size is 3024 × 1964 and the movie is 1920 × 1080."
100	- "The cursor file *name* was not attached: this is not a Frame Job cursor file…"
101	
102	A cursor file from a newer version of Frame Job gets the same alert, which says which version the file is.
103	
104	## Forget a cursor file
105	
106	Choose **Remove** in the **Cursor** section. The video stops using the file, as one undo step called "Remove Cursor File". The file itself stays on disk, so you can choose **Locate…** to bring it back. **Remove** is dimmed for a video with no cursor file.
107	
108	## When a cursor file has a problem
109	
110	A cursor problem never fails a recording or an export. You always get the movie, and Frame Job tells you what's missing.
111	
112	### While recording
113	
114	If a stretch's cursor file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why, naming the file:
115	
116	| The note says | What it means |
117	| --- | --- |
118	| "The cursor file *name* could not be written…", "…was not kept…", "…could not be put in place…" | The file couldn't be saved, or it failed the check Frame Job makes once it's written. No file was left behind. |
119	| "The cursor file for *name* was not written: no cursor was captured for it." | Nothing was captured for this stretch. |
120	| "The cursor file for *name* was not written: the screen never reported its start, so its times have nothing to count from." | Without a start time, the pointer can't be matched to the picture. |
121	| "The cursor file for *name* has only the geometry the screen had when it began…" | A file exists, but a move or resize of what was recorded after the start isn't in it, so the pointer can sit in the wrong place after that. |
122	
123	A stretch recorded **Separate** with no cursor file has no pointer at all, because it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
124	
125	### While exporting
126	
127	If a cursor file can't be drawn, because it's missing or damaged, the clip exports without a pointer and the export finishes as normal. The export's finish line counts the problem, for example "1 cursor warning (hover for details).", and hovering lists each one. The [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) shows the count on the job's row, with the same list in its tooltip:
128	
129	> The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …
130	
131	### In the preview
132	
133	A missing or damaged cursor file draws no pointer, and the preview says nothing. Check the **Media** tab, and use **Locate…** if the name reads "— missing".
134	
135	## Good to know
136	
137	- Moving a cursor file away doesn't take the clip's **Cursor** section with it. The section stays, and nothing is drawn until the file is back.
138	- Removing or re-pointing a cursor file doesn't touch the [settings on its clips](/recording/cursor-settings/). They wait for the next file.
139	
140	## With an agent
141	
142	An agent can read what a cursor file holds, which the app doesn't show you as a list. [`get_cursor_events`](/mcp/tools-recording/#get_cursor_events) returns a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts and stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path, ten times a second. Give it a media to read in the file's own time, or a clip to read in the clip's time, where each click and scroll also comes with its place in the clip's picture, ready for a zoom. It returns at most 5,000 rows at a time and says where to carry on. It edits nothing, runs on your Mac and needs no key.
143	
144	It won't read a clip that plays reversed, though it can read that clip's media, and it needs a media with a cursor file that's still on disk.
145	
146	[`set_media_cursor`](/mcp/tools-recording/#set_media_cursor) attaches, moves or removes a file as **Locate…** and **Remove** do, under the same check, and its `in_picture` value must match the file's. A cursor file belongs to the project's media, so giving the tool a `scope` is an error, and with a nest open the change applies to the whole project.
147	
148	[`record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/#what-it-answers) names each stretch's cursor file as `cursor_path` and any problem with it as `cursor_problem`. `export_status` lists a pointer it couldn't draw under `cursor_warnings`, and `render_frame` says so in its reply. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).
149

165	
166	Record shortcuts notes each keyboard shortcut you press during a screen recording, and when you type, so Frame Job can show those shortcuts on screen and speed up the typing afterwards. It never records what you type.
167	
168	<AtAGlance

170	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Record shortcuts"
171	  tools={['record_screen', 'get_cursor_events']}
172	  needs="macOS's Input Monitoring permission, and a display or a window as the source."
173	/>
174	
175	<Shot
176	  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
177	  alt="The New Recording panel with Source set to a display. Below Show Clicks is the unticked Record shortcuts box, with a note saying it records each shortcut and when you type, never what you type. Under it, the When it lands rows show Zoom in on clicks ticked, and Show shortcuts and Speed up typing greyed out."
178	/>
179	
180	## Turn it on
181	
182	<Steps>
183	
184	1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**.
185	
186	2. Set **Source:** to a display or a window.
187	
188	3. Tick **Record shortcuts**. It's off to begin with, and the panel remembers your choice for the next recording.
189	
190	4. Press **Record**. The first time, you'll need to [grant Input Monitoring](#grant-input-monitoring).
191	
192	</Steps>
193	
194	A note under the box says what it records. The box is greyed out for **Camera** and **Microphone Only**, which have no screen to go with the keys. It keeps its tick for when you go back to a screen source.
195	
196	While keys are being recorded, the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) shows a keyboard mark before the time, and its menu opens with a dimmed "Recording keyboard shortcuts" row. Everything lands in the recording's [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).
197	
198	## Grant Input Monitoring
199	
200	Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so pressing **Record** without the permission stops the recording from starting and opens System Settings for you.
201	
202	<Steps>
203	
204	1. Press **Record**. System Settings opens at **Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**, and the panel's note says what to do.
205	
206	2. Turn Frame Job on. If it isn't in the list, add it with **+**.
207	
208	3. Back in the panel, press **Record** again. You don't need to relaunch.
209	
210	</Steps>
211	
212	Frame Job asks for this after Screen Recording, and before the camera and the microphone. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) for all of them, and for what changes if you started Frame Job from a terminal.
213	
214	## What counts as a shortcut
215	
216	A key press is a shortcut when you hold:
217	
218	- <kbd>⌘</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> with any key.
219	- <kbd>⌥</kbd> with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc.
220	
221	<kbd>⇧</kbd> on its own never makes a shortcut, and neither does <kbd>⌥</kbd> with any other key, because that types a character: <kbd>⌥E</kbd> starts an é.
222	
223	A shortcut is stored with its keys spelled out, such as `cmd+shift+4`. The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`. The key comes last: a named key such as `return`, `tab`, `space`, `left` or `f5`, or otherwise the character the key types with no modifier, in lower case. `+` itself is spelled `plus`.
224	
225	## What happens to everything else
226	
227	Every other key press is stored as a typing mark, which is a moment in time and nothing more. It doesn't say which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all, and there's no mode that records what you type.
228	
229	A key held down until it repeats gives typing marks too, even if it began as a shortcut. Holding <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> is one shortcut and then a run of typing marks.
230	
231	## When nothing is recorded
232	
233	Nothing at all is recorded while any app holds secure input, as a password field does: no shortcut, and not even a typing mark.
234	
235	A password field that doesn't turn on secure input is different. Its keys are recorded as typing marks only, with no characters.
236	
237	Keys you press while the recording is [paused](/recording/pause-and-stop/) aren't recorded.
238	
239	:::caution
240	The keys stay out of the file, but the movie is still a picture of your screen. A password that shows on screen as you type it is in the recording.
241	:::
242	
243	## What you can do with the keys
244	
245	| Feature | What it uses | Where |
246	| --- | --- | --- |
247	| [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) | The shortcuts, shown on screen as you pressed them. | **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, or **Show shortcuts** in the panel |
248	| [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) | The typing marks, to find the stretches to speed up. | **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**, or **Speed up typing** in the panel |
249	| [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) | The typing marks, to zoom in where you typed. | **Zoom on typing** in **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** |
250	
251	**Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are in the panel's **When it lands:** rows, and they're greyed out unless **Record shortcuts** is ticked, because the cursor file would have no keys for them to use.
252	
253	## With an agent
254	
255	`record_screen` records keys when it's given `keys: "shortcuts"`. The default is `off`. It never asks macOS for the permission. Without Input Monitoring it won't start, and it names the System Settings pane, so someone has to grant it in the panel first. It won't record keys from a voice-over or a camera on its own. [`get_cursor_events`](/mcp/tools-recording/#get_cursor_events) reads the shortcuts and stretches of typing back. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#pointer-and-keys).
256

266	title: "Auto Zoom"
267	description: "Zoom a screen recording in where things happen, planned from its cursor file, with every zoom left as an ordinary action you can change."
268	---
269	
270	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
271	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
272	
273	Auto Zoom moves a screen recording in where things happen. It reads the recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), arrives at each click as it happens, stays while you keep working there, and zooms back out once you stop, so a viewer can see what you clicked without you zooming each moment by hand.
274	
275	<AtAGlance
276	  menu="Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
277	  where="Zoom in on clicks, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
278	  tools="auto_zoom"
279	  needs="A recording with a cursor file. Nothing else: it plans from that file on your Mac, with no picture analysis and no key."
280	/>
281	
282	## Zoom a recording
283	
284	<Steps>
285	
286	1. Select one or more clips of a screen recording. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** is available when every selected clip is a movie with a cursor file, and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.
287	
288	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" and **Zoom** is dimmed until they're read and there's a plan.
289	
290	3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls). The line under them [says what you'd get](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).
291	
292	4. Choose **Zoom**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
293	
294	</Steps>
295	
296	The whole plan is one undo step, **Auto Zoom**.
297	
298	## The controls
299	
300	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
301	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
302	| **Zoom:** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× | 1.25 to 4× |
303	| **Arrive:** | How long the zoom takes, in seconds. It starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click. | 0.6 s | 0.2 to 2 s |
304	| **Stay:** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it starts back out. | 2.5 s | 0.5 to 10 s |
305	| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | On | |
306	| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing as well as clicks. | On when the recording holds typing | |
307	| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. | Off | |
308	| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur. | On | |
309	
310	The number fields take up to two decimal places, and each value is held to its range.
311	
312	### Follow the cursor while zoomed
313	
314	When the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the zoomed view for 0.3 s, the view makes a half-second pan to it. It makes at most one of these pans a second, and none that would run into the zoom back out or a pan to a coming click.
315	
316	### Zoom on typing
317	
318	A stretch of typing is at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. The zoom arrives at the first key and aims at the last click before the stretch, because the typing marks say when you typed, not where. With no click before it, the zoom aims at where the pointer was.
319	
320	**Zoom on typing** is greyed out when the recording holds no such stretch. A recording only holds typing if it was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, which needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission.
321	
322	### Replace existing zooms
323	
324	Off, your own zooms stay, and a planned zoom that would meet one is [left out](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions). On, the selected clips' zooms go first. A zoom here is any action that changes only a clip's scale and position, so it takes hand-made zooms from [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) as well as Auto Zoom's own. A speed change, a fade or any other action stays.
325	
326	### Motion blur
327	
328	The zoomed clips get a 180° shutter in the same undo step, so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. Only clips that actually get a zoom are touched. A clip that already has a [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) keeps its own, and unticking the box doesn't take one away.
329	
330	## What the sheet tells you
331	
332	The line under the controls says what **Zoom** would do, or why it can't. It updates when you tick a box or leave a number field.
333	
334	| The sheet says | What it means |
335	| --- | --- |
336	| "5 zooms in 2 visits." | What **Zoom** would make. A [visit](#how-a-visit-is-planned) is one trip in and back out. Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out counts as one zoom, so a click with nothing after it is two. |
337	| "1 dropped where an action is already set." | Follows the line above: that many planned zooms [met an action](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions) already on the clip and were left out. |
338	| "0 zooms in 0 visits." | Nothing in the clips' played part calls for a zoom. **Zoom** closes the sheet and changes nothing, unless **Replace existing zooms** is on, when it still removes the clips' zooms. |
339	| "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas…" | See [A clip placed smaller than the canvas](#a-clip-placed-smaller-than-the-canvas). |
340	| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Auto Zoom plans only clips that play forward." | Auto Zoom only works on clips that play forward. Take the clip out of the selection, or untick [Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
341	| "Clip 12 has no picture." | The selection includes a clip with sound only. Select the picture. |
342	| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
343	| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
344	
345	With any of the last five, **Zoom** stays dimmed.
346	
347	### A clip placed smaller than the canvas
348	
349	Auto Zoom won't plan a clip that sits smaller than the canvas, such as a screen beside a camera or a picture in picture, because a zoom would fill the canvas. The sheet says "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto Zoom inside the nest."
350	
351	The way round this is to zoom inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), then place the nest:
352	
353	<Steps>
354	
355	1. Select the clip and choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.
356	
357	2. Open the nest. The clip keeps its small placement in there, so Auto Zoom gives the same message until you make the clip fill the nest again. Set its [scale and position](/canvas/transform/) back.
358	
359	3. Run Auto Zoom inside the nest. The zooms fill the nest.
360	
361	4. Leave the nest, and place the nest clip where the screen was.
362	
363	</Steps>
364	
365	Nest the screen before you shrink it and there's nothing to set back in step 2.
366	
367	## How a visit is planned
368	
369	Auto Zoom groups the recording's activity into visits, and each visit becomes a run of moves.
370	
371	- **A visit starts** at a click with any button, or at a stretch of typing when **Zoom on typing** is on.
372	- **The zoom in** ends on that first click or key, and starts **Arrive:** seconds before it.
373	- **A later click or stretch of typing** within **Stay:** of the last activity joins the visit. If it falls outside the middle 60 % of the view, the view pans to it, arriving on the click or first key.
374	- **The zoom back out** starts **Stay:** seconds after the last click or the last key of a typing stretch, and takes 0.8 s.
375	- **Scrolling ends a visit.** Three or more wheel events under a second apart count as scrolling, and the zoom back out starts where they start. A click after that begins a new visit.
376	- **Visits close together run on.** When one visit would finish zooming out less than a second before the next starts zooming in, the view pans across instead.
377	
378	The view keeps the canvas's shape and never shows past the edge of the picture, or of a crop on the clip. Near a corner it stops at the corner, so the click sits off centre.
379	
380	Only what plays counts. A click in a part you've trimmed away is ignored, and everything is placed through the clip's speed and any speed ramp.
381	
382	## The zooms are ordinary actions
383	
384	Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out is a normal [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/), the same kind [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) makes. Each is snapped to the frame grid and eases in and out. You can [move, resize or remove](/motion/change-an-action/) any of them, or [change what it animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
385	
386	Actions on a clip can't overlap, so a planned zoom that would meet one already there is left out and counted in the sheet. This goes piece by piece, so a visit can lose its zoom in and keep its zoom back out. Check those visits by eye.
387	
388	To try different settings after you've applied a plan, undo it, or run Auto Zoom again with **Replace existing zooms** on. Run again without it and the new plan meets the old one, and most of it is dropped.
389	
390	## Across a split
391	
392	The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording: clips side by side on one track, from the same file, each carrying on where the last stopped.
393	
394	- Every zoom back out returns to the first half's placement.
395	- No zoom crosses a cut. One that would is moved to one side of it.
396	- A zoom held across a cut carries into the next half, which starts already zoomed. Frame Job does this by setting that half's own scale and position.
397	- If that half wasn't selected, or has an action of its own during the zoom, the zoom goes back out at the cut instead.
398	
399	With **Replace existing zooms** on, a later selected half left zoomed by an earlier run goes back to the first half's placement, unless an action you've kept moves it.
400	
401	## What Auto Zoom remembers
402	
403	Frame Job remembers **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** from one use to the next. A value is kept only if you changed it and then chose **Zoom**. **Cancel** keeps nothing.
404	
405	**Zoom on typing** is never remembered. It's ticked whenever the recording holds typing.
406	
407	## Zoom when a recording lands
408	
409	**Zoom in on clicks**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), runs Auto Zoom by itself on a finished screen recording, with the values the sheet last used and no sheet. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
410	
411	## Good to know
412	
413	- A click right at the start of a clip has no room before it. The zoom in starts on the clip's first frame and takes its full **Arrive:** time, so it finishes after the click.
414	- **Zoom:** multiplies the size the clip is placed at, so a clip already scaled up goes further in than the number suggests.
415	- If the menu item is dimmed, check the selection. Recordings of a display or a window made in Frame Job have a cursor file. A camera's clip, a voice-over, a title and a movie from elsewhere don't, and one such clip in the selection is enough to dim it.
416	
417	## With an agent
418	
419	`auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments. An agent can also limit the plan to a stretch of the timeline, in which case replacing removes only the zooms in that stretch, and set a motion blur other than 50 %. See [`auto_zoom`](/mcp/tools-recording/#auto_zoom).
420

432	title: "Shortcut overlays"
433	description: "Show each keyboard shortcut you pressed while recording as animated keycaps on screen, at the moment you pressed it."
434	---
435	
436	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
437	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
438	
439	Shortcut overlays show a viewer what you pressed. Each keyboard shortcut in a screen recording appears as keycaps on screen at the moment you pressed it, so nobody has to guess how you did that.
440	
441	<AtAGlance
442	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
443	  where="Show shortcuts, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
444	  tools="add_shortcut_overlays"
445	  needs="A recording made with Record shortcuts on, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission. No key: it runs on your Mac."
446	/>
447	
448	## Add the overlays
449	
450	<Steps>
451	
452	1. Make the recording with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. It records your shortcuts and when you type, never what you typed.
453	
454	2. Select one or more clips of the recording. The menu item is available when every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.
455	
456	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**.
457	
458	</Steps>
459	
460	There's no sheet. Frame Job reads the cursor files, with the item dimmed while it does, and places one **Keyboard keys** graphic clip per shortcut on a [Shortcuts track](#the-shortcuts-track). Each sits at the bottom of the picture in the dark theme and shows for 1.5 s.
461	
462	The whole change is one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. If some shortcuts couldn't be shown, or nothing could be added, a [sheet says so](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).
463	
464	## What an overlay shows
465	
466	The keycaps pop in one after another, each is pressed in turn, and the group fades out at the end of the clip. ⌘, ⇧, ⌥, ⌃ and the arrow keys are drawn as symbols, a single character as its capital, and a named key such as `return` or `f5` as its word.
467	
468	## How overlays are timed
469	
470	**Where it starts.** An overlay starts on the frame where the press plays, following the clip's speed and any speed ramp. Only the part of a clip that plays counts, so a shortcut in a part you've trimmed away gets no overlay.
471	
472	**How long it lasts.** Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out. That minimum is (10 × keycaps + 25) frames at the project's frame rate:
473	
474	| Keycaps | Minimum at 30 fps | Minimum at 60 fps |
475	| --- | --- | --- |
476	| 2 | 45 frames, 1.5 s | 45 frames, 0.75 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
477	| 3 | 55 frames, about 1.83 s | 55 frames, about 0.92 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
478	| 4 | 65 frames, about 2.17 s | 65 frames, about 1.08 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
479	
480	**When you repeat a shortcut.** Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends doesn't make a second overlay. The first stays up until at least 1.5 s after the last press and carries a label under the keycaps: "×2", "×3" and so on.
481	
482	**When shortcuts come close together.** Overlays never overlap. A different shortcut pressed while one is showing takes over as soon as the first has had its minimum, and the first ends there. If that would show the new shortcut more than half a second late, it's left out, and a sheet says how many were.
483	
484	## The Shortcuts track
485	
486	Overlays go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when that track is usable, and otherwise on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. To be usable, the track must:
487	
488	- be in front of every selected clip's track
489	- be [unlocked and shown](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
490	- not be a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
491	- have nothing on it from the first overlay's start to the last overlay's end
492	
493	Inside an open nest, the track and the overlays go in the nest.
494	
495	## Change an overlay
496	
497	Each overlay is an ordinary graphic clip. Move, trim or delete it on the timeline, and change its keys, label, theme, position or accent colour in its [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). To change them all at once, select them first.
498	
499	The overlays are drawn by the project's own copy of the bundled [Keyboard keys template](/graphics/templates/). Frame Job writes that copy into the project's graphics the first time something is placed, and reuses it after. If you've [edited that copy](/graphics/edit-a-module/), it leaves your version alone and writes a fresh one beside it for new overlays.
500	
501	Undo takes the clips away but not the copy, which stays in the project's graphics for next time.
502	
503	## What the sheet tells you
504	
505	An informational sheet comes up when something didn't go as asked. Only the "too close" sheet comes with a change to the project.
506	
507	| The sheet says | What it means |
508	| --- | --- |
509	| "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added." | The part of the recording that plays holds no shortcut. Check that the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** on. |
510	| "1 shortcut came too close to show." | The overlays were added, without that many. With more it reads "3 shortcuts came too close to show." |
511	| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play forward." | Overlays only work on clips that play forward. Take the clip out of the selection, or untick [Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
512	| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
513	| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
514	| "The project changed while the cursor files were read, so no overlay was added. Choose Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays again." | You edited the project, or opened or left a nest, while the files were being read. Nothing was added. |
515	
516	## Show shortcuts when a recording lands
517	
518	**Show shortcuts**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), adds the overlays by itself on a finished screen recording, at the bottom in the dark theme. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
519	
520	## Good to know
521	
522	- Add the overlays before you run [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/). It keeps each overlay on a Shortcuts track at normal speed.
523	- Running the command again on the same clips doesn't replace the overlays. The Shortcuts track isn't free any more, so you get a second Shortcuts track with the same overlays on it. Undo first if you want to start over.
524	
525	## With an agent
526	
527	`add_shortcut_overlays` places the same overlays. An agent can also choose how long each one shows, from 0.5 to 10 s, put them at the centre or top of the picture, use the light theme, and limit them to a stretch of the timeline. See [`add_shortcut_overlays`](/mcp/tools-recording/#add_shortcut_overlays).
528

538	title: "Speed Up Typing"
539	description: "Play the typing in a screen recording faster, while speech and shortcuts stay at normal speed, as one undo step."
540	---
541	
542	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
543	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
544	
545	Speed Up Typing plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer doesn't sit through every keystroke. Frame Job finds the typing from the recording's cursor file, leaves anything spoken or any shortcut at normal speed, and makes the whole change one undo step.
546	
547	<AtAGlance
548	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
549	  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing"
550	  tools={['speed_up_typing', 'get_cursor_events']}
551	  needs="A screen recording made with Record shortcuts on. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
552	/>
553	
554	## Speed up the typing
555	
556	<Steps>
557	
558	1. Select the clip. Select both halves if you've split the recording, and any other recordings you want done at the same time.
559	
560	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" for a moment, with **Apply** dimmed.
561	
562	3. Set [**Rate**, **Shortest stretch** and **Keep pitch**](#the-settings).
563	
564	4. Read the summary under the settings, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s."
565	
566	5. Choose **Apply**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
567	
568	</Steps>
569	
570	The menu item is dimmed unless every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It's also dimmed while another sheet is open. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own clips and tracks.
571	
572	The edit is one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**.
573	
574	To do this for every recording as it arrives, tick **Speed up typing** in the recorder panel. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/#speed-up-typing).
575	
576	## What counts as typing
577	
578	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last. It lasts from the first key to the last.
579	
580	The keys come from the recording's cursor file, which only holds them if the recording was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Without it the menu item still works, but the sheet finds no typing. The file holds when you typed, never what you typed, and nothing is noted while an app holds secure input, such as a password field.
581	
582	Only typing in the part of the clip you've kept counts. Typing you've trimmed away is ignored.
583	
584	### Split recordings
585	
586	The halves of a recording you split are treated as one when you select them both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch. With one half selected, Frame Job only looks at that half.
587	
588	## The settings
589	
590	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
591	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
592	| **Rate:** | How much faster the typing plays. | ×4 | ×2 to ×8 |
593	| **Shortest stretch:** | Typing shorter than this is left alone. | 3 s | 1 to 30 s |
594	| **Keep pitch** | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch. Off, it rises like a fast tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | On | |
595	
596	The two number fields take up to two decimal places, and their values stay inside the range. The summary updates when you leave a field or change **Keep pitch**.
597	
598	Frame Job remembers these from one use to the next. It saves a setting when you apply the edit, and only if you changed it, so **Cancel** saves nothing.
599	
600	## What the sheet tells you
601	
602	The sheet says what **Apply** would do before you press it, or why nothing would happen.
603	
604	| The sheet says | What it means |
605	| --- | --- |
606	| "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s." | What **Apply** will do. |
607	| "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." | There's nothing to speed. **Apply** stays dimmed. Try a lower **Shortest stretch**. The figure in the sentence follows that setting. |
608	| "Waiting for speech detection on …" | Frame Job is still finding the speech in the files it names. **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet updates by itself. |
609	| "Speech detection has not finished for … Close this sheet and try again." | It waited 5 minutes and stopped. |
610	| "… is offline, so its speech cannot be read." | A file under a stretch is missing, so nothing changes. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) first. |
611	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Speed Up Typing cannot tell typing from talking." | Speech detection can't run here, so nothing changes. |
612	| "The typing from … cannot be sped up: …" | One stretch can't be sped. See [When it can't speed up](#when-it-cant-speed-up). |
613	
614	## What stays at normal speed
615	
616	Within each stretch, Frame Job sets aside every moment of speech and every shortcut, and leaves them at normal speed. What's left is sped up, if it still lasts as long as **Shortest stretch**.
617	
618	### Speech
619	
620	Any part of a stretch with speech under it stays at normal speed. That goes for every clip of a file with sound under the stretch, on any track, even if the clip is muted. So a voice on the Microphone track holds the typing back the same way sound in the movie does.
621	
622	The speech comes from the same on-device detection [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) uses. If a file has no saved speech, Frame Job saves it with the project in the same undo step. If detection hasn't finished, the sheet starts it and waits.
623	
624	### Shortcuts
625	
626	A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up. What stays at normal speed is the overlay's whole clip on a track named **Shortcuts**, or 1.5 s from the press when there's no overlay.
627	
628	[Add the overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) first, so that each one's full length stays at normal speed.
629	
630	### The edges
631	
632	Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends. **Shortest stretch** is measured before those edges come off. A 3 s stretch at ×4 speeds its middle 2.4 s down to 0.6 s, which saves 1.8 s. Cuts then land on frames, so the figures can differ slightly.
633	
634	## What the edit does to the timeline
635	
636	Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync with the screen and everything after moves up. A title or a graphic over a stretch is squeezed by the same amount, as Retime Range does it.
637	
638	The sound in a sped stretch is sped too, because it's cut and retimed with the picture.
639	
640	
641	## If a clip would go silent
642	
643	Rates multiply, so a clip already playing at ×2 goes to ×16 at a **Rate** of ×8. Frame Job leaves a clip's sound out above ×12, so when **Apply** would take a clip with sound past that, an alert asks first.
644	
645	**Set Speed** goes ahead. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed, so you can lower the **Rate**. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
646	
647	## When it can't speed up
648	
649	Speed Up Typing is all or nothing. If any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason in place of the summary.
650	
651	| What stops it | What to do |
652	| --- | --- |
653	| A locked track has a clip that ends after the stretch begins. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
654	| A transition touches the stretch. | Remove the [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). |
655	| Half of a detached pair is in the stretch. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
656	| A selected clip plays reversed. The sheet reads "Clip … plays reversed; Speed Up Typing speeds only clips that play forward." | Leave that clip out, or [turn off Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
657	| The cursor file is missing or won't read. | Use **Locate…** in the **Cursor** section of the Media tab. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
658	
659	A stretch can also be stopped by anything else that stops Retime Range, such as a nest clip or a caption page with timed words. See [When a range can't be retimed](/speed/retime-range/#when-a-range-cant-be-retimed).
660	
661	## With an agent
662	
663	`speed_up_typing` makes the same edit, with these differences:
664	
665	- It takes one clip or a list of clips, not both, rather than reading the selection.
666	- It can limit the edit to part of the timeline, which the sheet can't.
667	- It doesn't remember anything. It starts from ×4, 3 s and pitch kept unless told otherwise.
668	- It doesn't wait for speech detection. It says the speech hasn't been detected yet, and to try again in a moment.
669	- It never asks about ×12. The clip's sound is left out, and it reports that when it finishes.
670	
671	[`get_cursor_events`](/mcp/tools-recording/#get_cursor_events) reads a recording's typing stretches and changes nothing. See [`speed_up_typing`](/mcp/tools-recording/#speed_up_typing).
672

683	title: "Recording permissions"
684	description: "Which macOS permissions a recording needs, when Frame Job asks for each one, and what to do when one is missing."
685	---
686	
687	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
688	
689	A recording can need up to four macOS permissions, depending on what you record. Frame Job asks for them only when you press **Record** in the recorder panel, and never during a countdown.
690	
691	<AtAGlance
692	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security']}
693	  tools="record_screen"
694	  needs="macOS's Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera and Microphone permissions, as the table below says."
695	/>
696	
697	## Which permissions you need
698	
699	| Permission | Needed when | Where it lives in **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security** | Relaunch afterwards? |
700	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
701	| **Screen Recording** | You record a display or a window. | **Screen & System Audio Recording** | Yes |
702	| **Input Monitoring** | **Record shortcuts** is ticked and you record a display or a window. | **Input Monitoring** | No |
703	| **Camera** | **Source** is **Camera**, or **Record the camera too** is ticked. | **Camera** | Yes, after a denial |
704	| **Microphone** | A microphone is chosen, which every voice-over needs. | **Microphone** | Yes, after a denial |
705	
706	A camera on its own or a voice-over doesn't need Screen Recording.
707	
708	## When Frame Job asks
709	
710	A press of **Record** checks every permission it needs before the countdown begins, so a countdown never ends in a prompt. If one is missing, that press stops there, and the panel's note says what to do. The recorder panel is the only place Frame Job asks for these or opens System Settings for them.
711	
712	The checks run in a fixed order, and stop at the first one missing:
713	
714	| You're recording | The order |
715	| --- | --- |
716	| A display or a window | Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera, Microphone |
717	| A camera on its own | Camera, Microphone |
718	| A voice-over (**Source** is **Microphone Only**) | Microphone |
719	
720	Frame Job skips any that the recording doesn't need. Before any of them, it checks that you've picked what to record: a window, a camera, or a microphone for a voice-over.
721	
722	## Screen Recording
723	
724	The first press of **Record** without the permission shows macOS's prompt. The panel's note reads:
725	
726	> Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch.
727	
728	Turn it on, relaunch Frame Job, and press **Record** again.
729	
730	macOS shows that prompt only once, and Frame Job remembers it has asked. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane instead, and the note adds "System Settings is open at that pane."
731	
732	## Input Monitoring
733	
734	**Record shortcuts** needs Input Monitoring to see key presses. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it. So a press of **Record** without it opens System Settings at the pane, and the note reads:
735	
736	> Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +. System Settings is open at that pane.
737	
738	Turn Frame Job on there, adding it with **+** if it isn't listed, and press **Record** again. No relaunch is needed, and **Record shortcuts** doesn't need Accessibility.
739	
740	## Camera
741	
742	If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is sent anywhere."
743	
744	- Allowing it carries on to the microphone check and the countdown.
745	- Denying it leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the camera isn't granted.
746	
747	If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.
748	
749	## Microphone
750	
751	If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere."
752	
753	- Allowing it starts the countdown straight away, as long as the panel is still open.
754	- Denying it leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the microphone isn't granted.
755	
756	If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.
757	
758	## If you started Frame Job from a terminal
759	
760	A Frame Job started from a terminal or another app runs under that app's permissions, not its own. Turning on Frame Job in System Settings then makes no difference.
761	
762	The panel's note says so, and names the process that launched it by its process number (pid):
763	
764	> This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid 4182), so the grant that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or relaunch with open -a "Frame Job".
765	
766	Either give the permission to that app, or quit Frame Job and start it from the Finder, the Dock or `open -a "Frame Job"`.
767	
768	In a launch like this, Frame Job doesn't remember having asked. Each press without Screen Recording asks macOS again rather than opening System Settings.
769	
770	## The panel steps aside
771	
772	The recorder panel usually floats above other windows. While a macOS prompt or System Settings is up, it stops floating so that it doesn't cover them. It floats again when you allow a camera or microphone prompt, on your next press of **Record**, or when you open the panel again.
773	
774	## macOS's recurring alert
775	
776	macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record the screen. Frame Job can't see this alert, and the permission still reads as granted, so a capture waiting behind it looks like a recording that won't start.
777	
778	If the panel stays on **Starting…** and then says "The recording did not start within 20 s.", look for the alert on the screen. Answer it and press **Record** again.
779	
780	## With an agent
781	
782	`record_screen` never asks for a permission and never opens System Settings, because a prompt needs a person in front of it. It checks each permission it needs and, if one is missing, stops with a sentence that names it and says where to turn it on. Grant it once from the panel.
783	
784	If the recording doesn't start or finish in time, it reports that a macOS alert may be waiting. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
785	
786	## Related

795	title: "When a recording stops on its own"
796	description: "What Frame Job keeps when a camera, a microphone or the system stops a recording, and what to do when a recording can't be added."
797	---
798	
799	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
800	
801	A recording can lose a device or end without you pressing Stop. Frame Job keeps what it captured, adds it to your project, and tells you what happened. This page calls that adding "landing". It says what lands in each case, and what to do about what doesn't.
802	
803	<AtAGlance
804	  where={["The recorder panel's note", 'The menu-bar item']}
805	  tools="record_screen"
806	/>
807	
808	## Where you'll read about it
809	
810	Unless a section says otherwise, each case here is reported in the note on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back, but one with something to say does, as long as the panel was on screen when the recording began.
811	
812	If the panel wasn't on screen, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it and read the note.
813	
814	While a display or a window records, the panel is hidden, so the note only appears when the recording lands. While a camera on its own or a voice-over records, the panel stays up, so the note appears as it happens.
815	
816	## What's kept
817	
818	| What happened | Does the recording go on? | What lands |
819	| --- | --- | --- |
820	| [A camera on its own stops](#a-camera-stops) | No | What was captured |
821	| [A camera beside the screen stops](#a-camera-stops) | Yes | The screen, and the camera up to the stop |
822	| [The microphone stops](#a-microphone-stops) | Yes | The picture, and the microphone's file only if [it can be used](#a-microphone-stops) |
823	| [A voice-over's microphone stops](#a-voice-overs-microphone-stops) | No | What was recorded |
824	| [The display sleeps or goes away](#the-display-sleeps-or-the-system-stops-the-recording) | No | What was captured |
825	| [A stretch's movie won't read](#a-stretch-wont-read) | It has already ended | Every other stretch, and that stretch's voice if it reads |
826	| [A file is too short for a frame](#a-file-is-too-short-for-one-frame) | It has already ended | That file in the Media tab, and the rest as usual |
827	| [The recording can't be added](#the-recording-cant-be-added) | It has already ended | Nothing, but the files stay on disk |
828	
829	## A camera stops
830	
831	If a camera recording's camera stops, for example because it's unplugged, the recording ends there and what was captured lands. The note gives the reason, then "What was captured was added.":
832	
833	> The camera FaceTime HD Camera stopped on its own: it was disconnected. What was captured was added.
834	
835	It can also read "its session was interrupted", or give a reason from macOS.
836	
837	Beside the screen, a camera that stops doesn't end the recording. The screen keeps recording, what the camera wrote up to then lands, and the note gives the same reason. Anything you record after a later pause and resume has no camera. The one exception is a camera that fails while the recording is still starting. That stops the recording from starting, and the note gives the reason.
838	
839	If a camera hasn't settled at its rate when the recording begins, the recording begins anyway and the note says what it ran at:
840	
841	> The camera ran at 24.0 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway.
842	
843	## A microphone stops
844	
845	A microphone that stops partway through a screen or camera recording doesn't end it. The picture keeps recording and the panel's level meter goes silent. With the panel on screen, its note says so at once:
846	
847	> The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording.
848	
849	The picture lands either way. If the microphone's file didn't finish properly or won't read, it isn't added, and the note says why and where the file is, so you can [import it](/projects/import-media/) yourself. In a camera recording, a microphone that stopped on its own isn't added even if its file is whole. The same goes for a microphone that never started, which reads "The microphone never started recording, so the picture was recorded without it."
850	
851	## A voice-over's microphone stops
852	
853	A voice-over has nothing else to record, so if its microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, with a note:
854	
855	> The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped.
856	
857	## The display sleeps or the system stops the recording
858	
859	If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured lands, with the note:
860	
861	> The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added.
862	
863	Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar also lands the recording. The note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."
864	
865	## The screen is locked
866	
867	If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so a screen recording can't start until one wakes. The panel's note reads "No display with id … is shareable…", or "No window with id … is shareable." for a window. Wake or unlock the Mac and press **Record** again.
868	
869	## Resume doesn't work
870	
871	If **Resume Recording** fails, the recording stays paused and nothing already recorded is lost. Nothing new is recorded until a resume works, so you can try again, or stop and land what you have.
872	
873	The reason goes in the panel's note, for example "The recording could not be resumed: …". During a voice-over or a camera recording it appears there at once. During a screen recording it appears when the recording lands, and the panel comes back to show it.
874	
875	A **Pause Recording** that fails only beeps, because the recording is still running.
876	
877	## A stretch won't read
878	
879	Each stretch between pauses has its own movie. If one won't read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume, it's left out, and the stretches that do read land. The note gives the reason and names everything it left on disk:
880	
881	> A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …
882	
883	Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
884	
885	### Its voice still lands
886	
887	If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, on the Microphone track in the slot the picture would have had. The picture track keeps a gap there, and the next picture starts after it. The note reads "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture."
888	
889	That stretch's camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added.
890	
891	In a new project, a left-out voice from before the first picture has no timeline to sit on, so it lands in the Media tab without a clip, and the note says so.
892	
893	## A file is too short for one frame
894	
895	A file too short for one frame can't become a clip. It lands in the Media tab, the rest of the recording lands as usual, and the note says so:
896	
897	> … is too short for a frame (12 ms) and was added to the media list without a clip.
898	
899	## The recording can't be added
900	
901	If a recording can't be added, nothing goes on the timeline, but the files are safe. The note names every one, so you can [import them](/projects/import-media/):
902	
903	> The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …
904	
905	These are the usual reasons:
906	
907	| What happened | What to do |
908	| --- | --- |
909	| The project is at its limit of 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and the recording needs a new one. If the picture would fit but the microphone wouldn't, none of it is added. | [Remove a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/) you don't need, then import the files. |
910	| You were still dragging on the timeline. Frame Job waits for a drag to end, for up to 20 s, then reads "A drag was still in progress after 20 s." | Import the files. |
911	
912	If a file still hasn't finished writing 10 s after Stop, Frame Job tries to read it anyway. If it won't read, the note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the files kept on disk.
913	
914	## Very long recordings
915	
916	A recording longer than 9:59:59 carries on as usual, but the menu-bar item's label gets wider than the item was sized for.
917	
918	## With an agent
919	
920	`record_screen` reports all of this when it finishes, so an agent can tell what stopped and what landed: `camera.problem` and `mic_problem` say why a device stopped, `stopped_by` says what ended the recording, and `unreadable` lists any stretch left out, with the files kept and the reason. With the screen locked, it stops before recording and says that no display is shareable. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
921
